Author: Ping T.
Review: Several people raved about this place. After going there, I do not understand why. …MoreSeveral people raved about this place. After going there, I do not understand why.The pros:The service from the waiter is some of the best I've ever encountered in a KL restaurant, even in some of the top hotels. It's friendly, attentive, non-snobbish. Downright fantastic.The cons:The food. Don't get me wrong. The food is not bad. It's not fantastic either, it's just kind of slightly above average with a lot of frills to shill it as something extraordinary. They have a very fancy menu with reams of superlative information describing the food. Did you know that you can make any food sound fancy by adding the place of origin before the item itself? For example (this is not the exact item on the menu, just a demonstration of the style): Pan-seared Hokkaido scallops in Irish cream sauce, or Australian fillet mignion, served with Chilean asparagus or Tuscan rabbit or something (yes that was sarcasm). All these only serve to make the food sound more impressive than it is.There is even this really expensive dessert called 'An Ode to Newton' which has its own special card describing how it's anti-gravity and avant garde and all that, but basically is a scoop of ice cream on a wafer of flavoured ice on a glass of ginger beer. All for the bargain price of RM 25+This would not be such a bad thing if the portions were so minuscule for how much they charge you (RM 50-80 for a main). You order saddle of rabbit and you get one tiny little piece barely bigger a 50 sen coin. The duck breast was supposedly served with mash but what you actually get is a little dollop that looks like it had been served with a teaspoon.I don't mind paying for quality, but when a place is hyped but turns out to be so much style, and so little substance, it's really underwhelming. And honestly, if you paid 1k for one meal for a party of 5, I would have expected everyone NOT to leave the place hungry.The only way I'd ever recommend this restaurant to anyone if they and their wallet want a bit of weight loss, and if they enjoy the ambience and the prestige of having that kind of money to burn, I suppose.
Location: 6, Jalan 17/54, Seksyen 17, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Some cutleries were also missing from the set.For drinks, we ordered sake and Japanese green tea.The serving for the green tea was terrible to say the least. The waitress insisted on serving our green tea to the brim, which, is clearly not proper etiquette as serving tea to the brim gives an implication that you want a person to leave as soon as possible (she did so from the moment the tea was served)Part of the set was the dessert which was mochi ice cream and as my sister and I could not eat cold food, we asked whether it could be substituted for anything else. The waitress merely scoffed at us and said I don't think you can and proceeded to hurry us to make a decision whether we wanted the dessert immediately. She did not even consider going out to ask whether it was possible. On her part, I think this was extremely irresponsible.Food: 0/5Appetizer: bread was soggy as I said, fish roe was overcooked.Main courses:  The oyster was extremely slimy and was not fresh, sashimi too thickly sliced, not fresh; sushi was too big, could not fit in a mouthful; lobster was an absolute horror, I think I may see it in my nightmares... it was not fresh, part of the lobster meat had not been removed (it was the type where they took out the lobster meat and then cooked it before placing it back into its shell).Drink: 1/5The green tea was certainly not the type I'd expect in this restaurant, it tasted like those in perhaps, Sushi Zanmai? Really below expectations.The 1 point goes to the sake for tasting like a proper sake.Parking service: 0/5The valets messed up the keys and proceeded on a hunt for our car keys.

Author: Azrol
Review: Ishin, oh, Ishin. What a mixed bag of seeds. No doubt, one of the top rated Japanese Restaurants out there. I absolutely loved their 5 assortment of sashimi. Oh how clueless I was, this omurice was a landmine. I would've expected a restaurant as grand as Ishin to have the good kind of omurice - semi runny egg plated on fried rice with a spoon of demi glaze on top, finishing with some chives. Absolutely not. The egg was cooked all the way through, like some sort of fried egg you'd get at a school cafeteria. Add more to that, you put ketchup? With a name like Ishin? The atmosphere felt like I was in Japan, and you serve me ketchup? I know that's the normal way of doing it, but come on, there's a porch way of doing it if you didn't know. It's like ordering a cheese platter and getting the wooden board with grapes and a knife, but they using those pieces of processed cheese. All in all, I'd say it was a fine experience to try for yourself, but stay all clear from the omurice, maybe it's some kind of late april fools prank. Unless you want a bit of a taste of peasant food, then dive in. I say that with 100% legitimacy by the way.

I took her to eat her favorite eel; at that time, I came to know this Japanese restaurant in a detached house.The eel here is eaten three times—original flavor, seasoning, and soup. It's worth a try. The eel itself is grilled so that the skin is dry, the meat is soft, and the sauce is deep and not overwhelming; stir in diced green onion, mustard, and seaweed, and then add a touch of freshness; then add kelp bonito broth, the multi-layered umami immediately sweeps the taste buds Something.To be honest, the three ways of eating have their own characteristics and are all delicious. Although among the three, I slightly prefer the original way of eating, but as a person who is extremely resistant to the staple food of soup, #team擂茶 does not add soup, and the method of eating with soup makes it difficult for me to give up, or even to stop.The Kabayaki eel here has always been the most cost-effective choice in my mind in the past. Although the price is high, the portion is larger; although it is no longer the highest, it is still worth it. But looking back a few years later, maybe I changed. The Kabayaki eel here feels a bit too much sauce and a bit sweeter.As for sashimi, to be honest, quite disappointed. Regardless of the quality of the fish, the part or the skill of the knife, it feels that it is not at a level that matches the level of the restaurant. I remember that I was at a loss when I was eating.But what really got a little bit irritating was the king crab + foie gras dishes ordered by my friends.The king crab claw meat is covered with a thick layer of transparent starch, and the taste is similar to a tuft of potato flour when thickening failed, and then covered with greasy sauce, the deliciousness of the king crab is really submerged without a trace; and the goose The texture and taste of the liver itself is also not reflected-in my impression, this is really a 1+1 ≈0 dish that makes the raw materials false for this life.After the meal, I couldn't help but wonder: Is Ishin a Chinese-style Japanese restaurant?(Original)多年前生日 朋友从金宝下来跟我庆生，我带她吃她喜欢吃的鳗鱼；就在那时，我认识到了这家开在独立式洋房里的日本餐厅。这里的鳗鱼三吃——原味、拌料、加汤，值得一试。鳗鱼本身烤得外皮干爽、肉质酥软，酱香深沉而不泛滥；拌入葱粒、芥末、海苔，接着增添了一抹清新；再加入昆布柴魚高汤，多层复合的鲜味立刻就将味蕾席卷一番。说实在，三种吃法各有特色，也都很好吃。虽然三者之中，我略偏好原味吃法，但作为极其抗拒汤类主食的人来说 #team擂茶不加汤，加汤吃法让我同样难以割舍，甚至欲罢不能。这里的蒲烧鳗鱼，在过去一直是我心目中性价比最高的选择，价钱虽高，但份量更大；现在虽然不再见得最高，但仍然值得。不过几年后回头，或许是我变了，这里的蒲烧鳗鱼感觉酱汁有点偏多，也略甜了一点。至于刺身，说实话，相当失望。不管是鱼的品质、部位或刀工，感觉都不是和餐厅等级匹配的水准。比如三文鱼的脂肪分布差强人意，而很多鱼生都颇韧却一律厚切、没采用相应的切法，甚至带筋。记得当时我吃得一头雾水。但真正吃得有点来气的，是朋友点的帝王蟹+鹅肝料理。帝王蟹钳肉上裹了厚厚一层的透明淀粉，口感类似于勾芡失败时的一坨薯粉，再沾满油腻的酱汁，帝王蟹的鲜美真的淹没得无影无踪；而鹅肝本身口感和味道也没有体现——在我的印象里，这真的是一道1+1 ≈0，让原料虚妄此生的料理。一顿下来，我不禁都有些纳闷：Ishin是不是已经成了一家中式的日本餐厅？

Review: After dining at Kampachi's outlet in EQ, my partner and I wanted to try out Plaza33 to see if there were any differences in service and overall food quality + variety. Throughout the service, it was difficult to flag down someone to take our order and we were always told to wait. Once we managed to get hold of someone, we ordered everything possible so that we didn't have to go through the wait again. The variety is not as much compared to EQ (to be fair, the price is also lower here at RM178 per person compared to RM218 at EQ). The sashimi and most of the dishes were pretty good (especially the unagi, beef and halibut!), but sadly the grilled squid was not edible and had a really rubbery texture. It would've been a great experience if the service had been better. One thing to note, the green tea is priced separately and is not part of the buffet, so do expect to pay RM20++ extra for a pot of refillable green tea. We weren't told this, and were quite taken aback when the bill came.

Author: Donovan Tan
Review: This review is strictly intended for the outlet at Plaza 33. It's with a very heavy heart thay I have to give this review a 2 stars. Far from its glory days in Equatorial Hotel, where it's touted to be one of the best Japanese restaurants …MoreThis review is strictly intended for the outlet at Plaza 33. It's with a very heavy heart thay I have to give this review a 2 stars. Far from its glory days in Equatorial Hotel, where it's touted to be one of the best Japanese restaurants in Klang Valley. Had New Years Eve 2019 dinner with the family of which my parents are also long time patrons of this old restaurant establishment. Despite several warnings from family members and online reviews, we decided to give it another try. We ordered Toro, buri & salmon belly sashimi which turn out satisfactory. The Hamachi kama was nicely done too. Then we ordered a tofu yaka-something (can't exactly remember the name)... Batter on the tofu was Soo thick and sticky, we had to "peel" it off the tofu just to eat. It was bad. Very bad. Eel rice (Una don) for my dad was unappetizing and mediocre. A chicken teppankyaki set for our domestic help, a tai nyumen for myself and a shared chicken udon soup between my wife and my mum which was also terribly bland. The nyumen for myself is OK. Also, we ordered a kanpachi carpaccio which tasted fine. With my family complaining generally about the food, the ebi tempura arrives. Much to our dismay, the batter looks so dull yellow and heavy. After taking a bite, i decided to ask for the manager to lodge a complaint. You guys are Kampachi, not rakuzen( in fact I think comparing the dinner last nite, rakuzen does a much better job). We were more than willing to shell out a premium for the dinner., just because it's Kampachi. But to all standards, it wasn't worth it. Not at all. Paying about RM1500 for a dinner which is so bad, doesn't even do justice. With the EQ branch opened, I hope other branches are performing better. We did not order anything exotic, what we ordered were the basic staple menu of any respectable Japanese restaurant. I told the manager(Kevin is a nice guy btw), that if he, by his standard, can accept the tempura, I would pay for it. In the end we were not charged. We are not angry, we were just thoroughly disappointed that how can such a beloved establishment come to this or rather drop to these standards. Kevin even suggested to give them another chance and that before our next impending visit, to let him know so he can better prepare. With much respect to Kevin's goodwill, I feel, no matter who the patron is, all food standards and quality must be kept the same, at all time. Be consistent to all, not only to complaining guests. I would like to remind you, you guys are Kampachi, an establishment with a well loved heritage and history. When we pay "Kampachi" price, please give us "Kampachi" standard of food. Thank you for the complimentary mochi. I sincerely hope this review reaches the upper echelon management and that they will take this seriously. I do not usually write such a lengthy review, but only because Kampachi is a place of good memories and past experience. Yours sincerely.
Location: Petaling Jaya (North) P1-02, 1st Floor, Plaza @ Jaya 33, 1, Jalan Kemajuan, Seksyen 13, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Kareena Chhokra
Review: What an amazing dinner. 9 course omakase menu prepared by Chef Tetsuya Yanagida. Nothing overly complicated. Yana San let the natural flavours of the ingredients speak for itself and supported by the simplest and lightest of seasonings and …MoreWhat an amazing dinner. 9 course omakase menu prepared by Chef Tetsuya Yanagida. Nothing overly complicated. Yana San let the natural flavours of the ingredients speak for itself and supported by the simplest and lightest of seasonings and sauces. The feast began with a palate cleanser of fresh tomatoes which were sweet and crisp to the bite. This was followed by a gindara (cod) jelly infused with some other seasonings and flavours. Small but a good way to tickle the taste buds and get your appetite raring to go. This was followed by a tuna tataki topped with leeks in a very light soy based sauce. Melt in your mouth quality. This was my favourite dish of the night. Then came a clear soup with duck breast and shimeji mushrooms and red peppers. Very light and simple. This was followed by sashimi of salmon belly and yellowtail. Fresh and firm and not even the slightest hint of fishiness. Then came 2 more tuna courses of grilled tuna head meat and collar and a breaded deep fried tuna with a Japanese barbecue sauce. The fish in both courses stayed tender despite the cooking styles. The garlic fried rice that came after was an absolute yummer. Yana San then spiced up our taste buds with a spicy dip (no idea wat it was) and baguette. A simple stirfried shimeji mushroom dish with fried garlic followed. Apart from the omakase menu we also ordered king crab which was steamed and the crab legs meat was placed in a nori sheet with a sauce which Yana San prepared in front of us and served each one of us one by one. Dessert was the perfect end with a palate cleaning yuzu sorbet with mixed fruit and clear jellies. A really really good dinner overall and pretty healthy actually come to think of it. Yana San himself is a really pleasant character and it's obvious he has deep love for what he does.
Location: Lorong Utara C, Pjs 52, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: GOH Philip
Review: A splendid breakfast.Excellent set up and ambience.I sat beside a fountain and it was cooling and relaxing whilst i wait for my …MoreA splendid breakfast.Excellent set up and ambience.I sat beside a fountain and it was cooling and relaxing whilst i wait for my start of day.Waitress mixed up long black n americano. But her growth mindset really made my day as i explained to her the difference between the two.My word, her paitience was impressive as she was willing to hear out a bored gentleman such as i.I ordered the big breakfast and was immidietely taken aback by its generous portion.I went through the dish , savoring everything in sight.Lets go through the plate together now.The home made hashbrown was fluffy and crisp, infused within the potato , was a bit of corriandor , which to my suprise , gave it quite a bit of character.The greens were fresh and seemingly plucked from the pot as it was crunchy and the plants were enchanced with olive oil, giving it a smooth texture.The mushrooms at the side were splendid as well, they were chewy and flavourful , sauteed with care so that the moisture within it was not lost on the pan.Next is the Eggs, well seasoned and scrambled without dryness , it could be eaten without any additional salt, making it one of my favourites on the plate. Its helping was really generous as well, covering almost 30 percent of the plate.Sampling the wheat and grain toast was marvelous, its crunchiness really stood out from the rest of the soft and chewy dish. Pairing with a helping of eggs was a delight as it encouraged the bread the absorb some moisture from the egg, making it a wholesome bite.Last and not least, was the pork sasauge . It was amazing and a burst of flavor as it filled my mouth full of salty goodness , the juicy meat was one thing, but the flavor that came with it was indiscribable, making it the main protagonist of the lot.The price as well, was reasonable and in good ratio with the quality food they had produced.Coffee was subpar, but the food made up for the experience.I give it a 5 stars , not only because of the food. Hygiene and ambience was well done and the table set up was interesting.Kudos to the chef and serving team.P.goh signing out.

Author: Andrew Attan
Review: The menu is big on the wall or can be downloaded online.  Service is very good, a tad over the top.  13 of us spent RM47O, including 6 cups if coffee.  We even got a free slice of cake on the house! (We shared our feedback on the food too) …MoreThe menu is big on the wall or can be downloaded online.  Service is very good, a tad over the top.  13 of us spent RM47O, including 6 cups if coffee.  We even got a free slice of cake on the house! (We shared our feedback on the food too)The breast meat of the Chicken Sandwich (RM24) was too dry and the creamy sauce felt like those ready made bottled sauce.  Served on sourdough, the dish is functional but not delightful.  The Grilled Chicken (RM26) was slightly better with a balsamic sauce but the chicken was on the dry side.The Beef Kebab (RM30) was not so bad but felt precooked and warmed in the microwave.  The beef was not juicy but it had flavours. Salad dressing can be improved.  The cherry tomatoes were sweet!The Panini with bacon (RM26) was the best of the lot we tried! Bread was toasted perfectly (a bit blackened) with lots of butter.  There was a bit of a sweet sauce that provided a very nice balance to the fillings.  Came with chips.Fish and Chips (RM28) were good.  They used New Zealand Dory and the fish was firm and not soft and melty like other low grade fish.  Never knew there were different "breed" of dory fish! The batter was thin but firm and served hot.Pizza (RM26) was alright.French fries were very well done.  Served hot, the bite was awesome.  Salad lacked proper dressing.The Long Black (RM11) and Capuccino (RM13) was alright.  A bit more on the strong side.Overall, food items prepared on the spot, like fish and chips and panini, were excellent.  Others, prepared in central kitchen and warmed on site, were less desirable though not atrocious.Food quality, service, decor and general feel is consistent across the MidValley and Atria outlets.  A place we would have at least coffee or a meal every time we are in KL.
Location: G37 & GK1, Ground Floor, Atria Shopping Gallery, Jalan SS 22/23, Damansara Jaya, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Low Dywin
Review: We recently headed over to Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara to try the menu at Nizza – the hotel’s new specialty French – Mediterranean restaurant. Nizza is a refined contemporary yet casual French Riviera-inspired restaurant, with modern …MoreWe recently headed over to Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara to try the menu at Nizza – the hotel’s new specialty French – Mediterranean restaurant. Nizza is a refined contemporary yet casual French Riviera-inspired restaurant, with modern interior architectural – with light colours playing off in its interiors and a striking blue-and-white flooring. The chic pool deck ambience outside meanwhile is reminiscent of the coastline of Cote d’Azur with modern glass parasol pool bar, comfy beach cabanas, and low modular seating.The restaurant has a show kitchen where you can watch the chefs whip up a variety of specialty items a la minute. This 135-seat restaurant features a variety of seating arrangements, and is suitable for intimate dinner for two, to communal tables for groups of four or more, depending on the occasion of course. The tables are interspersed adequately apart so you won’t hear what the other table is saying while the ambience has an emphasis on unique finishing ranging from highly-detailed art deco and ceiling mural to exotic lightings and a wine cellar with a good selection of wines.On the menu are a whole range of dishes including Duck Liver Pate, Marinated White Anchovies, Nizza’s Garden Salad, Summer Niçoise Salad, Cheese Board, Garlic & Herb Crusted Spring Lamb and White Sturgeon Caviar. Among the recommended dishes are Turkey “Salchichon”, Truffle & Mushroom Croquettes, Garlic Prawns, Bouillabaisse Cote De Opal, Charcuterie Board, Salted Baked Whole Snapper, White Sturgeon Caviar as well as the Provencal and Lamb Sausage Pissaladiere. Hand-crafted cocktails and fine wines are also available to complement the cuisine.Verdict- cafe latte 5*
Restaurant: Nizza Restaurant @ Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara

Author: G U Renukanand
Review: Probably the best Italian restaurant in Damansara. I have heard so much about this place and finally got a chance to bring my family there. …MoreProbably the best Italian restaurant in Damansara. I have heard so much about this place and finally got a chance to bring my family there.A great selection of Italian food and pasta which is made at the restaurant. So you are not getting any cold frozen pasta reheated and served in a platter.Kicked off the evening with. zucchini parmagiana , typically you would get a eggplant but here they have replaced it with zucchini. Both vegetables add such an unique experience to the dish. I was expecting a baked dish but this was served in three portions and topped with freshly grated cheese.Next up was the Burrata on a plate of cherry tomatoes tossed in olive oil,  balsamic vinegar and fresh greens. The fresh creamy Burrata and the sweet cheery 🍅 were a treat in the mouth.Who doesn't love a good 🍕. This was our main course for the night. Started off with a four cheese pizza and then ended up ordering another Margarita pizza. At this point the chef came to our table and explained how each dish is specially made. He was quick to point out that there is less than 2% yeast in the dough and they allow the dough to raise over a 3 day period.I have to say it was one of the best pizza dough we have had in Kuala Lumpur. Crusty on the outside with a pillows of air bubbles all over.The chef didn't want us to leave with having tried his pasta and we were treated with a small portion of Ricotta cheese and spinach tortellini with a butter sauce. We were licking the sauce out of our fingers. It was just incredible.The Italian chef is an avid travelled with experiences from all over the world.A dinner for 2 could easily be in the range of RM 150-200 with wine and with desserts it can be upto RM 250.If you are seated outside and the weather is pleasant it's a treat. Do call for reservations as they are usually packed for dinners. Most patrons enjoy the meal and are not rushed to finish the meal for the next customer.Great service and attention by the team at Nero Nero.On not to forget the Lemoncello which was served to us in the end 😘
Location: L3 - 02, Jalan Damanlela, Damansara City Mall, Damansara Town Centre, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur

Tables were pretty cramped …MoreCame here for a Valentine's and Anniversary celebration.First things first, the seating plan was awkward. Tables were pretty cramped together and neighbouring tables could definitely hear your conversations. It wasn't too comfortable especially during Covid season were we should be spaced out even more so with our masks off.We ordered the Wagyu Teppan Course. Wanted to try the Seafood Teppan Course but they said lobster was out of stock that night. The time taken for the food to be served course by course was satisfactory, not too fast and not too slow, just enough time to enjoy the food. The sashimi was fresh and my favourite was the Halibut & Hokkaido Scallop. The main course however, was a bit underwhelming as the beef was too fatty and way undercooked even though we were asked our preferred doneness. The dessert was also a bit underwhelming as it was just a scoop of ice cream with some fruits. With the price paid I would've expected more.The floor staff that night was very attentive and friendly. For the service I have no complaints, we were very well taken care of.Overall I would say Iketeru is a nice place. But if you want a very nice experience or a romantic dinner I would suggest looking elsewhere as the food experience and price paid doesn't match up in my opinion :)

Review: Dined at the restaurant for dinner when the hotel newly opened. It was amazing at the time. After a few years had a birthday lunch booked for my wife. After a few years had a birthday lunch booked for my wife. The experience was less than amazing and the price we paid not quite justified. When I called I asked for a quiet table and also the possibility of a small slice of cake to be arranged. Surely not a big ask for a 5 star hotel of that reputation and size. When we arrived the place was quite busy with a business clientèle lunch crowd. We were given a choice of a table in the middle of the dining room or a tatami table which was not ideal with a 2 year old child. During the booking asked for a child seat as well which obviously with the not pre defined table was not prepared either. No acknowledgement by the waitress either during arrival of my wife's birthday so I guess either the message was not passed on or they were just too busy. Staffing was not adequate as there were other employees from other departments helping out which was easily noticed due to the different uniform. For lunch sets ranging from RM150-300 each in average the meal was mediocre. The sushi set we ordered had small pieces of sushi which resembled nothing you have in Japan or other more traditional Japanese restaurants in KL. The soup was not very tasty and flavourful. The dessert was jelly with diced fruits which were taken from the waiter station near the sushi bar evidently suggesting that it was sitting there for a prolonged amount of time. Overall very disappointing and kind of subdued the occasion. There are better place out there where for the price you feel that you are getting a meal in an ambience you will enjoy with a higher quality of food and attentiveness of service.

But she replied in a rude manner that the restaurant is fully occupied today and she is being kind enough to come and serve us and etc ? Review: Dine in here on 16th September after months of lockdown.When first arrived at the restaurant, we were greeted with warm smiles and they …MoreDine in here on 16th September after months of lockdown.When first arrived at the restaurant, we were greeted with warm smiles and they followed strict SOPs and guidelines.The decor is not bad and we had a lovely seat by the window.My girlfriend and I ordered "Fish and Chips" and Salmon. Not going to lie, their fish and chips is one of the best ones I had in KL. Perfectly fried, crispy on the outside and soft in the inside. The chips were thin and they were just cooked right and with a nice balance of salt. The tartar sauce was a nice touch to it as well. The salmon was also very unique, its cooked as if was like a steak, its just melt in the mouth and came with a sweet and savoury sauce. Love the decoration on the plate. The mash potato that came with it was also one of the best mash potatoes I had. Fried tempura Spinach leaves also added a nice touch. The portions are great as well.For desserts, we ordered their famous strawberry cheese mille crepe cake, very unique presentation. It came as in a crepe form instead of a cake. It was heavenful. The flavours are not too overpowering each other and it has a right balance of sweetness.The waiters were attentive and friendly as well. They always come by to fill up our water glasses.Price is reasonable. Food is great. Exceptional customer service.10/10 would come here again for special occasions.

Or u could make a mistake, like me, of placing an order at the counter, with the staff being under the impression that u want a takeaway. In any case, u had to wait for what seemed like decades for something as simple as mushroom soup. And if u had ordered dessert, like an ice cream, it would arrive together with the food, inappropriately. I had to tell the staff to keep the ice cream till I'd finished my soup. The lychee drink I had contained enough sugar to ensure both my legs were amputated by the end of the meal. I then tried a cake, which happened to let me down with its indifference. It was neither good nor bad, just indifferent,which any decent foodie will tell u is a fate much worse than either. I fared better with the mini Hokkaido cheese tarts, which were quite decent although I'd probably suggest ppl to avoid the ordinary and salted caramel ones, and go instead for the chocolate ones, covered in peanuts. The place was undermanned, obviously with one staff busy doing the baking leaving the other to attend to u. After this somewhat irregular experience, I thought SR had indeed come down in the world.

I had ordered the big breakfast and it was …MoreFirst of all, the service is excellent. Many servers welcomed us on my way in and lead me very quickly to our table. The menu had a lot of variety but that did not detract from the quality. I had ordered the big breakfast and it was delivered very quickly to my table. The first thing I tried were the mushrooms which were plump, juicy and bursting with flavour. They claimed the hashbrown was homemade and the quality confirmed that with a slight hint of acidity not found in frozen hashbrowns. Their scrambled eggs were exactly what you would expect; you could practically slurp them like noodles. The salad which paired very well with the hashbrown lacked the acidity which would have made the dish somewhat unpleasant. The bacon was lovely, not too salty and a wonderful texture that was not too chewy nor crispy and the fat was kept to a minimum. Finally, the artisan bread was a highlight, being just the right texture and a subtle flavour to finish off on. I highly recommend this place to anyone driving through Bangsar in search of a good plave to eat.

Author: Michelle
Review: The infamous VP nasi lemak ! Always busy always packed to the brim . The queue moves fast and the turnover is fast so fret not. Plentiful of seating upstairs and downstairs. …MoreThe infamous VP nasi lemak ! Always busy always packed to the brim . The queue moves fast and the turnover is fast so fret not. Plentiful of seating upstairs and downstairs.Affordable meal that is consistent in taste! I guess that is why most people go back to them as they know what to expect! Food is served very fast so if you want to grab a quick meal, it is convenient.It may not be the best Nasi Lemak in town but whatever they are serving is definitely good enough to serve the mass market.Many times we have been there, the taste of the chicken has always been the same - it is very well flavored and managed to retain its moistness. I went to the one who said will bring the cake `shortly' and requested for bill. Also I told him to cancel the cake. But he said sry sir. I'll bring it now. I mean this how you treat your customer? If you can't open your kitchen sharp 6pm. Pls don't promise to your customers. So they won't be waiting or they might find some other alternatives. But the cake part is totally unacceptable, its not like you're baking a new fresh piece of cake. I wonder why it took almost 15mins. Cake was serve within the mention duration since I complained. Or else it might have taken even more time.Please teach your waiter what is the definition of 'surprise'. Your waiter just came and saying infront of my gf I'll give complementary cake since we overlooked your booking. Wth, I request cake for my gf birthday not as complementary item. Author: Lia W

I'll share my experience on why I say so.Noise level: 3/5Ambience: 4/5Price: 3/5Lighting: Dim and romanticService: 4/5Disclaimer: So I've read reviews on this place. Seems like authentic Italian restaurants are scarce in KL and this is a place that people like.However, I have a bone to pick with how information is relayed.Look at the pics I've included: menu & pizza, notice the price of "Via Del Pre Kul" - RM51 description says "Tuna belly, capers, olives..." Looking at this, we thought that it would be fresh frozen tuna belly like either fillet or some other kind of tuna belly ya know? Not canned tuna!! I mean, look at the price of this pizza compared to the other pizzas. However, it came in tuna chunks - canned tuna no less.I WAS PEEVED. Plainly put, I think the menu is misleading especially for someone who loves tuna. I LOVE tuna more than salmon lol.I have to give it to the server though, we asked 2 servers - 1 of them NEVER came back to me, the other server answered without hesitation when I queried why the menu said tuna belly and it came as canned tuna.Thanks to the manager, Mr Maury, who clarified that the tuna belly was canned tuna belly. He even brought the can out for us to see. Bless his soul.TLDR: I think the server should tell customers that the tuna belly is canned tuna belly for "Via Del Pre Kul" - RM51, before they confirm their order. I don't expect the management to revamp the menu because of this single reason.
Location: 25, Lorong Setiabistari 2, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

The kothu …MoreA Sri Lankan restaurant with a fine dining experience. Being their specialty, we had expected better quality of the crabs (especially with rm 180/kg being charged). One is never enough.One more thing, the lassi is unreasonably overpriced even for a fine dining restaurant. If you add the service charge and gst it comes up to a whopping RM25.50 each.

Author: Azimeer Manaf
Review: MTR is a vegetarian South Indian restaurant located in Brickfields. This restaurant chain started back in 1924 by 3 brothers in Bangalore and the set up a new standard for Indian restaurants by adopting European standard of hygiene and …MoreMTR is a vegetarian South Indian restaurant located in Brickfields. This restaurant chain started back in 1924 by 3 brothers in Bangalore and the set up a new standard for Indian restaurants by adopting European standard of hygiene and cleanliness when the brothers visited Europe.The restaurant in Brickfields continued this standard and it is reflected in their cleanliness. I was super impressed with the washroom, it is very clean and dry, so unlike most asian restaurants. The servers are attentive, polite and fast.Food wise, is consistent and made fresh upon the customer making the order. We had the masala dosa and the rawa masala dosa. The dosas were just heavenly, after lathering it with the clarified butter. It was a definitely filling breakfast. Although I have tasted a better coconut chutney elsewhere. A highly recommend place if you are particular about service and cleanliness, plus to food is good too.

Author: Andy Low
Review: Fatty Crab Restaurant specialises in preparing sour and chilli crabs.The restaurant has more than 30 years of history and is known as 老字号 to the many …MoreFatty Crab Restaurant specialises in preparing sour and chilli crabs.The restaurant has more than 30 years of history and is known as 老字号 to the many agreeing locals.We arrived at around 645 PM and was met with many hungry customers at the restaurant. My friend and I quickly took our place at a small table for two and count our blessing that we did not have to wait very long.We ordered 3 dishes; a single crab, fried rice and chicken satay.The sour and chilli sauce is tasty and has been prepared with love and care.The sourness add a punch to the dish.It has been thickened with flour so that it mixed and adhere to the crab meat easily.What impressed me most about the dish is the freshness of the crab! This aspect of the dish is a clear standout for me.The fried rice is a disappointment to me. It is clearly curated to match the crab dish.It is a touch bland to me perhaps they do that to match the sourness of the crab sauce but I would have like it to be more salty.I would suggest them to try Japanese rice to make the fried rice. The stickiness and inherently sweetness of Japanese rice will add to the appeal of the dish especially when match up with the crab.My favourite dish surprisingly is the most humble of the 3 dishes. The satay were made slightly shorter than normal and is succulent. Making biting a pleasure and a less than mouthful experience.The last bit that is worth mentioning is the restaurant is very clean by normal standard.I would scored it 5 out of 5 stars. However, for a coffee shop environment with no AC the price of the dinner came up to be 140RM. Too expensive to me.
Restaurant: Fatty Crab Restaurant 肥佬蟹海鲜楼

Author: Joanne Nicole
Review: Great food and efficient service. Was here on a Saturday night and it was packed. The numbered waiting system with a call signal on a screen is such an effective method. After 20 minutes waiting we got our seats even when we had arrived at …MoreGreat food and efficient service. Was here on a Saturday night and it was packed. The numbered waiting system with a call signal on a screen is such an effective method. After 20 minutes waiting we got our seats even when we had arrived at 7.35pm.Xiang loong baos were excellent as usual. But the star had to be the scallion sauce dry la mian which we ordered with shredded pork and prawns. The la mian was pulled until nice and springy, plus it wasn't overcooked so it still had a 'QQ' bite. The scallion sauce was aromatic with the fragrance of fried shallots. We had the stir fried pea shoots, which came with a good wok hei. We loved it so much we ordered another bowl.The only minor let down that night was the House Special appetizer; the dressing was too heavy on the sesame oil so that was all we could taste, resulting it being the only dish we didn't finish that night.I have to also mention our dessert. We had the black sesame rice ball (tang yuan) in both red sesame soup and soy milk. We were blown away by the tang yuan as they were generously filled with black sesame paste, which was not well balanced in sweetness. We preferred the one in the soy milk as it too wasn't too sweet and was light enough to balance out the. Again, we ordered another serving.All in all despite the crowd, we had a great meal at DTF. The servers came over as soon as they spotted us waving at them. They responded briskly and worked with great efficiency. A great place to return to and well worth the high ratings.
Restaurant: Din Tai Fung 鼎泰豐 at The Gardens Mall
Location: Lot LG 207 & 208, Lower Ground Floor, Lingkaran Syed Putra, Mid Valley City, Kuala Lumpur

Go to Singapore's Tony Roma's and have their ribs and you'll know what I mean.The ribs here are okay. Not exactly melt in your mouth / fall off the bones immediately type. I do like their soy sauce chicken even though it tends to veer towards the sweeter side. But this sweetness goes really well with the flavorful chicken meat.Tofu with shimeji mushrooms and spinach bathe in minced meat sauce. This was the first time I ordered this dish because I felt like trying something new from the menu. I didn't regret my choice at all as I lap up the whole dish with the rice that my mother did not finish even though I had already down my wantan noodle. The minced meat sauce really made the dish.The dry wantan noodle though came in a pool of sauce so I began to wonder whether I ordered dry wantan noodle or wet wantan noodle. Thankfully the sauce was not sickly sweet like that of Annie's from PJ. So all was good in the end.

Review: I understand this place has been around for more than 2 years and there isn't enough publicity of it. While I haven't tried their savoury dishes or their desserts, I can certainly vouch for their sourdough breads though, which was the main reason of my visit.I'm sold with the cosy ambience and the proximity of the place to housing estates in PJ. There's certainly not enough of bakeries of such capacity, and quality. And I'm certainly sold with the sourdough bread! The honey oat sourdough I had was pillowy soft, a joy to chew on and the oats gave the crust a beautiful texture in contrast to the soft inside.If you knew the benefits of sourdough bread, you may not want to eat other breads again. Sure, the price of an average sourdough bread in the market may be a put off to some compared to the industrial baked loaves. However, The Kitchen Table's sourdough breads are priced quite fairly between RM9 - RM14 per loaf. Mind you, the bread making process of a sourdough bread is complex and the most unique part of it is the fermentation process which gives it a robust flavour! People suffering from Celiac disease or those with intolerance to gluten may want to consider a well-baked sourdough bread as this old fashioned recipe has proven to break down gluten in wheat and inadvertently makes sourdough bread safe for consumption for this group of people.Sourdough Bread: 4.0/5Ambience: 4.5/5Service: 4.0/5Cost: $$ (Sourdough), $$$ (Others)

I didn't want the refund as it was a small amount. Hence I requested to add on another item from the menu which costs the same amount. Staff was kind and honest to point out that based on my current order, adding the requested item would be too much and thoughtfully suggested to replace with a dessert from the menu even though it is pricier than the refund value as a gesture of apology as well. I happily accepted. Delivery was quick, as I requested immediate delivery upon order, meal was ready and collected by Grab Express 15mins after order and payment were finalized (1 appetizer, 4 individual ala carte mains with rice and sides, 1 ala carte grilled prawns, 1 dessert). Delivery arrived within 20mins after collection. Estimated distance between restaurant to destination is about 12km during dinner hours. A little confusion from the delivery guy who seemed to expect me to pay him the toll fare he spent for the delivery..... Food was delicious. Prawns were ok. Not consistent in terms of freshness. Everything was packed with flavour except the Bebek Mepanggang, needed more seasoning we reckon. The 2 varieties of Sambal were really good. Choice between spicy and really super spicy 🔥. Portion sizes were acceptable, however, could be bigger for the price point per dish. Dessert was ok. Not too sweet but will not purposely order it. Overall, an enjoyable dinner. Family approved. Thank you Uma Bali.

Author: Amelia Liew
Review: This is my first time at the Ganga Cafe (Seapark branch), a vegetarian Indian restaurant. My kids ordered roti tissue and roti canai, while I went for tosai cheese. The tosai cheese is a winner for me in terms of look and taste. You can't …MoreThis is my first time at the Ganga Cafe (Seapark branch), a vegetarian Indian restaurant. My kids ordered roti tissue and roti canai, while I went for tosai cheese. The tosai cheese is a winner for me in terms of look and taste. You can't really tell from the photo which I've posted here, but the tosai had a nice, even coloring/cook throughout, and there was enough cheese (mozarella) in the tosai to satisfy me as opposed to the other ones I've tried. That said, if you like TRUCK LOADS of cheese in your tosai/naan like I do, go for Steven's Corner; trust me, you will be in cheese heaven. As for the coconut and tomato chutneys that accompany the tosai dish, I can't say it did much for me; I am still of the opinion that Kanna Curry House at Seksyen 17 PJ still serves the best chutneys in town. As for the roti canai, again, it has that nice, even coloring like the tosai, and mighty crispy too. On to the roti tissue, my daughter didn't really like it because they have doused some sweetened condensed milk over it, which was not noted in the menu, but otherwise, it tasted fine. If I ever drop by the area, I certainly don't mind visiting the cafe again to try their other dishes.P/S: The toilet is super clean; definitely a plus point in my book!

Review: Vegetarian Indian restaurant. One of the few places that sells chaats in Petaling Jaya. The staff and chef might be from overseas (this place and for many indian eateries)  but i do not think they are being paid high salaries for Malaysian standards. Maybe  the food execution is a little better at the finer places but.... .So they opened this branch in a pj location known for affordable eateries.  We thought we'd give this a try for dinner after passing by several times. It was disappointing. Simply put.. expensive and small servings. No aircond or maybe a little. No fine cutlery or tableware.   Fast service? Yes... Well..  The shop is never ever fully patronised because of its high price in a cost conscious neighborhood unlike its other place. Clean? Yes when compared to regular eateries.Ordered the millet or some special grain chappati which came as 2 small chapatis with small servings of sukhi bhaji and dhal cha from the server's curry sauces heating trays. I think it was at least RM5 for this. Gasp! Whats so exclusive about small portion food thats not completely cooked fresh? Ok... You can tell me the chapati is fresh from the skillet... from a premix batter.I did not make a complaint about a hair strand i found in the potato bhaji.There was nothing special about the potato or the dhal.Also had several mini bite size puri which tasted ok but... expensive.Also an over priced vegetarian nasi lemak...honestly... I could be wrong but if it was foreign indian chefs who cooked it... Then it should not be for a true Malaysian tongue. At least use fresh santan and/or use more la since charge high price. Measly peanuts. Sambal was ugh. Perfect the dish before putting it on the menu.Of course...  The owners want you to order the even more pricey 'special' dishes to truly savor the ganga experience..... I could but from what i have tried...No thanks2 stars because it offers clean eating environment. 1 star for food.

The room is completely pitch black and you can't even see your ✋ in front of your face.Guys, if you're coming because of the food and easily irritated for not knowing what you're eating then don't waste your time here. The food actually is delicious but I know some people can't stand or are picky about what they're going to eat. Have heard of an experience where someone was very frustrated spending so much and unable to see if you've finish everything on your plate.Completely enjoyed my time and meal experience, felt like a kid try new foods again. Just try to not have expectations and you will surely be happy you went.More on the food: we had the vegan menu. I appreciated so much that DitD KL had an understanding of veganism and had readily available vegan options. And they are improving all the time, I imagine.Appetizers were the best. True five stars! Soups were solid, mains were good. The deserts we not imaginative, unfortunately. We were really looking forward to them, but were a bit disappointed: cut up bananas, canned lychee were used to replace the cheesecake and the brownie respectively (from the regular menu). Hey, at least we can be sure it’s all vegan!Still, we thought the food was great overall. The chefs are doing their best to accommodate vegans and we really appreciated that effort here. I guess it goes along the lines of the general energy of this place: we are all equal and we all deserve respect and a possibility to exist comfortably and happily. Glad to support this.Service: top notch, with a touch of family warmth. Perfect from start to finish.Ambiance: lovely venue (coincides with a jazz bar), great soft instrumental music playing in the dark room, spacious veranda to relax on and digest the experience.Bottom line: ideal for dark first timers! Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Nowhere offer dishes like Mum's PlaceTheir menu comprises a blend of Malay, Portuguese, Chinese and a smattering of …MoreNowhere offer dishes like Mum's PlaceTheir menu comprises a blend of Malay, Portuguese, Chinese and a smattering of nyonya and Indian dishes which makes them a favourite among diners since 2001. But 20 years on, they have decided to call it a day as the Covid-19 worsened and doing business in Malaysia is very tough.So this post is dedicated to the couple who have been serving delicious and homey food to the Malaysians for 2 decades. Please visit them and try their dishes before they are gone for good.◾Otak-otak cubes served with Thai sauce - a good snack while waiting other dishes to be served.◾Assam pedas Parit Jawa Jenahak - spicy, sourish and appetising dish made popular by Maharani town of Johor◾Sambal Sotong with Petai - who doesn't love petai?◾Lemak kuning pedas sotong - love the coconut milk that doesn't made me jelak. Squid was cooked just right.◾ Portuguese "Devil" Curry chicken - might be spicy for some but to me it was OK.◾Chicken Pong Teh with sauce, potatoes, black mushroom - classic nyonya dish that I will order everytime I see one in the menu.◾Bitter gourd with prawns & chicken◾Kampung style fried rice with telur mata kerbauP.S: They are closing down at the end of 2021 so do visit them before they migrate to Australia.
Location: 31-1, Jalan PJU 8/5a, Damansara Perdana, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Aishwarrya Krishnamoorthy
Review: This was my very last meal in Malaysia before I flew off to further my studies. 😩 I decided to dedicate my last food experience in Malaysia to Mum’s Place as this was one of my family’s usual dinner/ family gathering spot whenever we …MoreThis was my very last meal in Malaysia before I flew off to further my studies. 😩 I decided to dedicate my last food experience in Malaysia to Mum’s Place as this was one of my family’s usual dinner/ family gathering spot whenever we wanted a good Malaysian meal. I think I’ve been dining there for easily 12 years+, and since I haven’t had their delicious home styled cooking in a while, I ordered some of their signature dishes:1. Lemak Kuning Jenahak Fish - This was by far the most disappointing one. The sauce was so dilute and sour. It tasted worst than the normal Malay roadside stalls. For the price they’re charging, they should really put some effort to improve their taste as well as enforce quality control. Whilst the fish was fresh, the way the chef cooked it just ruined it all. You could barely taste anything but sour lime water.2. Four Angle Beans with Belacan - Hmmm, there was no belacan paste to my surprise 😱 It was just oil and a hint of sour paste which was so watery that you couldn’t distinguish between the gravy and oil. I think the chef woke up on the wrong side of bed because everything was sour, watery and just disappointing overall.3. Chinese Style Omelete - "Foo Yoong" Tan - We previously used to order this all the time whenever we ate here. However, today they really reduced on the no. of prawns, onions and vegetables inside the egg. Their egg foo yoong used to be the best because it was loaded with ingredients, but now it’s just a plain omelette with a few thin sliced onions and one prawn 😤Overall, I can say that the good memories of this place is long gone. I was always very fond of this restaurant as it tasted very homely and comforting which leaves you reeling for more. But today sums up how much they’ve slacked from the last I went.    If only good restaurants can maintain their quality and taste till the very end… 💔
Location: 31-1, Jalan PJU 8/5a, Damansara Perdana, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

The outside was crisp with sea salt, whilst the middle was perfectly medium, giving a crisp texture whilst melting like butter in the mouth to leave a feeling of warmth and completeness.I would highly recommend DC.

Author: Philip Rom
Review: Took the 5-Course Meal with wine pairing (1 white, 1 red).Ambiance: Restaurant's exterior is almost understated you'll miss it. Gives you …MoreTook the 5-Course Meal with wine pairing (1 white, 1 red).Ambiance: Restaurant's exterior is almost understated you'll miss it. Once your table is ready you'll be led to the actual restaurant area upstairs. The dining area is relatively small but still gives you a sense of coziness with the lighting. The cold pasta with bafun uni was just heavenly - silky, luxurious and just rich without being overpowering.I highly recommend if taking any of the meat dishes as main, order the additional pan seared foie gras. The combo with the meat is just a match make in heaven...the foie gras, crisped on the outside from the searing just melt in your mouth faster than butter.And if you're a cheese lover - don't even think twice about the options for dessert... just go for the cheese cart. You get to pick 5 different type of cheeses. My date and I are cheese lovers so we got to try 10 different types of cheeses. And it's not the typical cheeses you will get from your local store. Exotic, eye-closing cos it's so good type of cheeses. We had 5 light and 5 strong cheeses. It was served with 2 pcs of bread, nuts, orange jam, and raisins.Price was RM1400++ for 2 pax inclusive of 2 glasses of wine each. Expensive but you will not regret the experience if you value this kind of experience.Service: Attentive. Pleasant and jovial. Staff are knowledgeable on the wines and the cheeses, and can also offer good recommendation.Would definitely come back again!

Hospitable as …MoreA long overdue review of a memorable evening early this month ! Flawless in every way ! Glad to revisit after a long hiatus from them ( DC has in fact been our go to place for celebrations of all sorts since its opening). Hospitable as ever, Restaurant Manager Yann takes note of all my requests, even gets back with better table option just the night before our dinner.As usual we go for the Discovery Menu for a full on indulgence. Big up to a tremendous sprint on food presentation - clean and pristine. NEAT! The flow and rhythm of the scrumptious spread of premium seasonal offers are well orchestrated and coherent. The execution is confident and suave, unassumingly sophisticated without overly manipulating the ingredients. An unsung hero worth mentioning is their palate cleanser, never a plain dull concoction in DC ! This time we have : pumpkin/ ginger/ lime/ hazelnut/ semut flower -mind bowing combo awaking all senses for the subsequent dishes. As it was a birthday celebration, they even presented us a special Birthday dessert (on top of what are already in the menu), a marvellous take in transforming a single ingredient, glutinous rice, to a phenomenal interplay of all forms and textures.Chef Darren even personally serves one of the courses - an admirable gesture for any chef of his standing.Mature as they are in the market, they maintain humble, ready to embrace constructive feedback at all times - they don’t wait, they ask, always going the extra miles! From appetizers to desserts, every bite is effortlessly luscious and mesmerising. Coupled with exquisite customer service, DC is a definite all-rounder as a fine dining experience.

They never mention that infant and kids are not allowed for fine dining.Please learn to handle situation like this. I walked out of the restaurant and called another "Fine Dining Restaurant" and explained the situation to them ( They Need To Make Reservation too before you can dine, preparing the table). They happily said, come over and they will prepare the table for us. We had nice Japas dinner and a very nice view at KL. It was just 10 minutes from DC, they prepared the table before we reached and just direct us to our table. They said, yes fine dining needs time to prepare, but with efficient staffs it can be done in 5 minutes and rules can change and of course Infants and toddlers are allowed and they can eat their own cooked food in a fine dining restaurant.The thing here is that, although its fine dining, you cannot ask me to go away just because the pax count did not tally with reservation.Google review asked me the question would you go there again.Definitely No, avoid at all cost. Author: Nabil
Review: Had a very nice lunch here. Overall, it was a very efficient and delicious experience. …MoreHad a very nice lunch here. Overall, it was a very efficient and delicious experience.We were greeted by Ms Ashikin who directed us to our reserved table. Some choices of chinese tea were then offered; we chose pu-erh tea.Next, we decided to try the Peking Duck dish. It wasn't a long wait till we see the Peking Duck being delivered to us in a nice "cage". The duck was then efficiently carved tableside by Ms Ashikin. For the duck's second dish, we chose to stir fry it with black pepper.The duck rolls tasted delicious both with and without the hoisin sauce. The crispy duck skin and the juicy duck meat make a pleasant textural contrast which we enjoyed very much. The stir fried duck was also very flavorful; spicy, salty and sweet.Finally, we were offered the dessert menu by the head waitress. Both of our dessert choices gave a wonderful end to our Peking Duck lunch.

Author: Calvin Lim
Review: One of the best Bak Kut Teh you can find in this earth as Bak Kut Teh is a Malaysia dish so I think there’s no better BKT outside of Malaysia. If you do not want to/have time to travel all the way to Klang to find a good and authentic Bak …MoreOne of the best Bak Kut Teh you can find in this earth as Bak Kut Teh is a Malaysia dish so I think there’s no better BKT outside of Malaysia. If you do not want to/have time to travel all the way to Klang to find a good and authentic Bak Kut Teh, this is the place you can go. The soup is super good, the taste is super authentic with the correct ratio and types of herbal, it is salty enough to eat with literally everything. You can dip fuzok, you tiao, or any vegetables into the soup and it will taste good. Price is a little bit expensive compare to other store but the portion of the meat they give is more than normal store. Review: That instinct to search for a ‘lepak and makan’ makes Kuala Lumpur an especially fun place to live and eat - the city’s charming urban fabric are famous for hiding all manner of culinary riches. …MoreThat instinct to search for a ‘lepak and makan’ makes Kuala Lumpur an especially fun place to live and eat - the city’s charming urban fabric are famous for hiding all manner of culinary riches.One such ‘makan place’, the Malai Thai Cuisine at the Fraser Place KL, had its potential for charm. Located neatly in the middle of the golden triangle KL, it’s a walking distance from our office as well as all the main attraction around from KL Tower to KLCC to Bukit Bintang. If you driving there, they have valet service at your disposal.Malai is Thai name for a flower garland that you will almost certainly see everywhere in Thailand. It’s a symbol for luck and respect. We were told the restaurant is barely few weeks old, yet the staff is polite and attentive to our food order, which is part of what makes Malai so delightful.Having heard the head chef is a native Thai’s who combined traditional thai with a twist of modern flavor, we decided to try few combinations and shared across the table. We start with a spring rolls, followed by Gaeng keawwaan Thai green curry, deep-fried shrimp with tamarind sauce and stir-fry mix vegetable to name a few. The service is quick, the food served with fresh ingredients with great flavours, intensely aromatic, and kind of mesmerizing when paired with spicy Prawn Tum Yum.We finished the lunch with sticky rice drown in fresh coconut milk, and sweet Thai mangoes on the side. It was a lovely combination of flavours and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Can't fault this. Simple, and wonderful.. Presentation on point, taste is beyond expectation.

We took the XL since we were sharing; it was definitely not what you would expect when you hear XL 😅 I would suggest the restaurant marks it as "for 1" & "for 2" or "starter" & "main" instead of S and XL which gives false expectations.Service was also weird. Then they did it again, this time to my credit card!!! I mean, after accepting a payment, most people would gather the receipts and hand the card back to you nicely, but this guy literally chucked,  like tossed! my credit card into the basket that contained the after dinner mints. What the heck?Sadly, for a place that charges rm45-80 per main, they're falling a bit short.

Review: For the longest time I always thought that The Daily Grind serves only burger. Well, I was partly correct because they specialise in burger and particularly beef burger, although there are other options too. And that was what I got to taste (their other-than-burger dishes) when I didn't know what to eat after shopping in Bangsar Village.Even though they are located on Lower Ground level, the restaurant is actually visible from the main road. Note: I was actually utilising my Entertainer privilege (Buy 1 Free 1 main course) which was not applicable for burgers so we ordered mostly non-burger items except for one a-la carte item.◾O'mega Salmon - Pam seared salmon steak with light & tasty sundried tomato sauce & sauteed vegetables. Doneness was perfect and as requested. A good change using sundried tomato sauce.◾Rosemary & Lemon Roasted Chicken - perfectly half roasted chicken with sauteed tomatoes and charred romaine lettuce. They nailed this dish with tender and juicy chicken meat with some citrus note.◾Seafood Mac & Cheese - classic Mac & Cheese but with added fresh seafood. Added sweetness from the seafood incorporating with the cheesy sauce.◾Seafood spaghetti - gotta love the savoury garlic broth coating the Al dente spaghetti and fresh seafood.◾Classic chicken burger with cheese - reasonably thick and  juicy chicken party with melted cheese on top & a great set of buns, but not a breast in sight.I was pleasantly surprised with the quality of food here. Perhaps next time I'm back here again I'll try their non-beef burger.
Location: LG8 Bangsar Village, 1, Jalan Telawi, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Anastasia Soh
Review: Best Promises Are The One’s Which We KeepFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-in …MoreBest Promises Are The One’s Which We KeepFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-inService: We placed the order via Whatsapp and was greeted by a polite & informative customer service who made pretty good recommendations.Packaging: From a by-stander’s point of view, not knowing what was within, it looks more like a beautifully wrapped gift set emitting an extremely seductive scent of truffleSpring Signature (RM 198)1 x Dried Longan Bread Loaf1 x Truffles Butter (100g)1 x Kulim Butter (80g)1 x Soup of the Day1 x Mushroom & Summer Truffles Penne1 x Saute Vegetables2 x Pomme Puree with Homemade Duck Bacon1 x Pumpkin Puree2 x Slow Cooked Duck Leg1 x Torched Baby CabbageTaste: The promise of providing a no-frills personalised dining experience at an affordable price, seems ambitious but Skillet has begged to differ. Just the amount of food that came out from the box alone was enough for us to go back & take a second look at the receipt. Portions were fit for a royal banquet, presentation & plating was more of an art. After recovering from having been run over by the charging smell of truffle, we dug into the banquet laid before us.The freshly baked dried longan bread emitted a crunch as we peeled it apart to reveal the soft fluffy texture within. The thought of the juiciness of the duck finished off with a touch of cranberry makes us hungry all over again. The penne was al dente with a sprinkle of freshly shaved truffle accompanied by a rich & creamy mushroom sauce. The texture of the soup of the day was creamy & had a rich flavour of broccoli delighting the diner with each spoonful.We concluded the meal with a customized Cempedak tart fulfilling their promise of a personalized dining experience.Price: Reasonable for the quality & variety of foodRecommended? Though some may say they were trying to hard, we think they were simply delivering their mouth watering promise in the form of a gift box set to lift one’s spiritsOur full review is on Instagram (@monk3yseendo)

Author: Cheah

The wait staff did his best to explain each dish as it was being served but it was rather apparent he was just regurgitating what he was told to memorize and sounded really anxious. I don't blame him but I feel the entire dining environment was a bit try hard. None of the floor staff showed enthusiasm, knowledge or passion towards the food they were serving - sort of defeats the whole fine dining concept.I would have given a 3star rating, but i was mainly concerned with the hygiene and some of the little things I observed while dining there made me a little squirmish and uncomfortable. In a Covid-19 time like this, I would expect places to up their game on hygiene but was honestly slightly shocked to find that that cutleries were set directly on the table. I tend to be skeptical about the cleanliness of tables in general, so I actually got them to change my set.My side plate also had residual food stuck to it 😐 got them to change that too. Appetiser was served in a wooden tray of beans, with the amuse bouche placed directly on the raw beans. Again, in a time like this, I get a bit worried as to how clean this wooden box is, whether or not the same decorative beans were used to serve previous customers and if so, did any kid or patron previously digged their fingers and played around with these very beans. Perhaps I'm a bit paranoid but I tend to take notice on small things like this.I would have let it slide a little more if it was at a more casual diner, but given Skillet's reputation and the price you're paying, I expected a much higher level of hygiene.

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Seafood Galore in PJFor those who love seafoods especially in PJ - I do - chances are high that …MoreSeafood Galore in PJFor those who love seafoods especially in PJ - I do - chances are high that you've gone to Unique Seafood at some point of your life. Located along the main road of Jalan Kemajuan in the industrial Section 13 area, this restaurant has been one of the focal point of seafood lovers for many years already. I, for one, had come here so many times that I'd lost count.Walk into the spacious restaurant with one section filled with tanks containing various live seafoods to choose from. From clams to prawns, geoduck to lobsters, king crabs to fish, there bound to be something that strikes one's fancy.Service is considered good for space this big although there's always room for improvement.Seafood selections:◾steamed mud crab - what's better way than steamed to enjoy its sweetness and original taste? Bonus is when I flipped that shell to find roe inside.◾Tiger prawns in superior soy sauce - my favourite dish everytime I come here. Gotta love the sweetish & sticky sauce enveloping every inch of the prawns.◾steamed oysters with garlic and glass noodle - another default order because somehow I think that they make better version of this style compared to other restaurants.Their non-seafood dishes also deserve mention:◾roasted salted chicken◾Mongolian style venison meat - the son proclaimed that this was the best venison he'd tasted.◾stuffed chicken skin with fish paste and almond flakes - not many places offer this dish due to the tedious process but Unique Seafood does.◾claypot chicken - the young ones need something with gravy hence this dish, surprisingly it was so good that the parents fought with them.◾Deep fried enoki mushroom - addictive snacks to crunch on while waiting the dishes to arrive.◾Ginger & spring onion venison meat - good but Mongolian got the vote.◾Braised beancurd in pumpkin sauce - my least favourite dish because the sauce was rather bland.◾fried rice - packed with essential wok hei, I couldn't resist stealing a few spoons despite that I hardly take carb.◾Stir fried black pepper udon with seafood - the slurping sound confirmed that this dish was good.If privacy is your concern, they do have several private rooms with minimum spending - and some comes with karaoke system to sing your lung away. Just call ahead to make reservations because they are always packed especially during weekends.Parking is readily available in the basement or there's valet to park your car for you (at a fee of course) so that you can walk straight into the restaurant.
Location: LOT 9B-3, Jalan Kemajuan 12/18, Seksyen 13, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Review: We reguraly visit steak houses when on city trips in Asia and were particulary attracted by the aged meat that this restaurant specialises in.Interior is nice, wine selection is good. We booked a table in advance and were …MoreWe reguraly visit steak houses when on city trips in Asia and were particulary attracted by the aged meat that this restaurant specialises in.Interior is nice, wine selection is good. We booked a table in advance and were a bit disappointed to find out that they gave us a small table for two, immediately at the counter, with noise from the kitchen and many passing waiters. People who book for two, for a dinner, especially when booking in advance, usually prefer a bit of intimacy...The biggest disappointment however was the meat. Firstly it was served almost cold. We had ordered "rare", but there are ways to ensure that rare is at least served lukewarm.Then there was the meat quality. We ordered Angus T Bone steak Rib, not the cheapest on the menu, 600grams each. Although the taste was good, parts of the rib eye came with many tendants. Other parts on the steak were too aged in our opinion and almost had no texture anymore (it had become a soft mash and almost fell apart like a mashed potato).We paid 800 RM for the two of us. 1 bottle of wine included, no starters, no desserts. For that price tag we would have expected the high quality that we came for.Next time in KL we will go back to some other great steakhouses that we discovered in KL.Our conclusion is based on our experience of yesterday evening. We did not taste other meats than the Angus T Bone steak. Based on this, our feeling is that Beato either has to reduce its price tag, or to increase its quality.Disappointing experience.

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: A self-taught chef, Ahong, caught the market by storm when he opened up a restaurant serving high-end grade food at affordable price. I mean, where else can you expect a competently executed 300g NY Strip at less than RM60? Or 300g Wagyu …MoreA self-taught chef, Ahong, caught the market by storm when he opened up a restaurant serving high-end grade food at affordable price. I mean, where else can you expect a competently executed 300g NY Strip at less than RM60? Or 300g Wagyu Flank MB4-5 at less than RM150?To be honest I don't really eat beef so I've no comment on the meat. My visit to Grub by Ahong was purely for their other dishes. Being my first time, I didn't know what to expect but it turned out that (almost) everything have to be self-served.Ground floor is where all the kitchen action is - after registering, you'll be guided to your table where you have to scan, order and pay for your food via Beepit. Just wait for everything to be sent to your table - easy peasy lemon squeezy! This eliminate the need for more manpower thus cutting the cost which will then be passed down to the happy customers.◾Grub Signature Salad - love the addition of orange for that citrusy taste together with various fruits and salad; plus oriental dressing and the option to add either grilled chicken or striploin (at a cost of course). Good start to the dinner!◾Fried French Quail with Red Salsa - when it's fried, my concern will always be the doneness as I don't like my poultry to be too dry.. good thing was that it was done beautifully. The red salsa proved to be a good dipping sauce, but I added another green spicy chutney + yoghurt sauce to experiment with different flavour.◾Grilled lamb - lovely medium grilled lamb racks doused with sauce, salad and potato on the side.◾Bring your own wine... They don't charge by bottle, instead they charge by glass at RM5.00 per glassPlease bear in mind that this is a no-frill restaurant, so do not expect a high-class romantic dining environment. You get what you pay for.. and extras will be charged if you want more.
Location: 608, Jalan 17/10, Seksyen 17, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Sharon C
Review: Good food, decent prices, subpar service. If you like instagrammable food, this place is not for you. …MoreGood food, decent prices, subpar service. We said ok and informed that we would be there in 10-20mins. We arrived 20mins later (8.10pm) but were made to wait 25mins (8.35pm) because, and i quote, "Your table is not ready yet." Location: 608, Jalan 17/10, Seksyen 17, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Julian Lee
Review: This place was said to be so notorious that you couldn't even get a table without a reservation. If you come here with high expectations of table service then I'm sorry to say you will be disappointed. Everything down to the cutlery and …MoreThis place was said to be so notorious that you couldn't even get a table without a reservation. If you come here with high expectations of table service then I'm sorry to say you will be disappointed. Everything down to the cutlery and water is self service. They have the kitchen floor and the air conditioned floors above. Take a board when you go in, order and fill in your table number. Get your cutlery and drinks; wait. Most will be turned off by this but the place let's you know its the food that does the talking not service. My first taste of Wagyu was mediocre to say the least. Since moving on from my teenage years, I never order well done. Today it's medium rare and It ticks all the spots- tender, juicy and no gaminess (cow smell) but that was it. I didn't feel the oomph or feel good factor and now sitting down, I think I've figured out why. I'm so used to the gamey smell that without it, I felt something was missing. This wagyu was devoid of the gamey smell which is the characteristic of the meat, hardly the fault of the chef. The 300g Wagyu Flank will set you back RM95 whilst the cheaper Wagyu Rump will set you back at RM85 which is not exorbitantly expensive if you have tasted kobe beef. Suggest those interested in a no frills dining, to reserve a table during dinner or walk in for lunch. Fame and fortune is around the corner do act fast. EDITED: they now have tableapp, you will need to go to Facebook, select the dates and pay RM15 deposit per person. Make sure you remind them about the deposit when paying for the bill.

Author: Fyf
Review: The foods were very good in taste, portion size and pricing. Got the Spaghetti with Crispy Chicken Chop. The spaghetti has lot of mushrooms and cooked well, just in the menu it was said that it’s creamy pesto based sauce, but the pesto …MoreThe foods were very good in taste, portion size and pricing. Got the Spaghetti with Crispy Chicken Chop. The spaghetti has lot of mushrooms and cooked well, just in the menu it was said that it’s creamy pesto based sauce, but the pesto taste was not quite there. The chicken chop served with it is crispy and the sauce is Sriracha mayo, but the side salad was fantastic, freshly served with balsamic vinaigrette.Satay was big and used very juicy and tender chicken cubes, satay sauce was decent but can be a bit too sweet. Belgium Milk Chocolate was so chocolatey and the Salted Egg Croissant was filled with so much sweet and salty salted egg sauce, and the pastry itself was soft and flaky. Lemonade was fizzy and very refreshing.Service was great too despite coming very late for iftar at 7pm and all of the tables are full except one for both of us. I’m surprised that the food came up quite fast despite the late order. Only the drinks came later after the foods arrived. But one of the waiter accidentally inputted our salted egg croissant order for the chicken satay when we didn’t order one. He apologised for his mistake and said he was willingly to pay the satay, but we refused and said we will pay for it. He courteously said thank you and appreciate for the kindness. Even other waiters came to us, apologised for the mistake and offered discount for the satay.Overall, it was a very pleasant experience. Great food especially the portion, and impeccable service. Only I didn’t manage to picture the interior as my table was next to the entrance. Will I come again? For sure it’s a yes!
Location: 53, Jalan Sultan, Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Review: Went here to tapau my coffee. Service-wise: very courteous ladies, and attentive waiter too. The shot pulled for the long black is weak, especially since it's for iced long black. Review: I am on the fence when it comes to this restaurant as I had a mixed experience when I visited. My friend and I had lunch there on a Friday afternoon and the place was full. Since I had arrived first and my friend was only a few minutes …MoreI am on the fence when it comes to this restaurant as I had a mixed experience when I visited. My friend and I had lunch there on a Friday afternoon and the place was full. Since I had arrived first and my friend was only a few minutes away, I went in to grab a seat first.I relayed my request for a table for two to a waitress, who brushed me off and tried to usher me to a bar seat. I repeated that I would prefer a table and didn't mind a wait. Just then, a small table in front of me vacated so I quickly asked the waitress if I could have it, and she just shrugged, "Yalah, if you want," before walking off to leave me and the still-unmade table.I quickly grabbed a seat and luckily managed to get the attention of another waitstaff to get it cleaned. My friend arrived then and we both ordered from a waiter. Food arrived quickly as it was 2pm the lunch crowd was emptying. We both had ordered a salmon sashimi set and I was (happily) shocked to see that each sashimi slice was literally thicker than my thumb. There were ten gigantic chunks on ice, miso soup, chawanmushi, salad and a bowl of rice - all for only RM38. I spent the whole meal in shock at how much value I was getting.But sashimi aside, the food taste wasn't anything to shout about. The chawanmushi, while generous with the minced meat added, was too heavy with the miso/dashi flavouring so the eggs tasted way too earthy instead of light. We had also ordered some clams nabe, which was a bit too salty. But at least the sashimi was reasonably fresh, although I wish they had done away with the grey flesh.Overall, Edo Ichi does have reasonable set meals, but keep in mind that their ala carte options are significantly pricier. So I'd advice to grab their value set meals for lunch and dinner. The next time I return, I'll just stick to their sashimi.
Location: No.7, Unit G4 Ground Floor NEXUS, Jalan Kerinchi, Bangsar South, Kuala Lumpur
