Author: Kevin Kok
Review: Overall, the ambience is good, service is good, food is acceptable.Environment, it has a good ambience that is suitable for family, friends, and …MoreOverall, the ambience is good, service is good, food is acceptable.Environment, it has a good ambience that is suitable for family, friends, and even a date. Other than that, the tables are clean as well.Service, it is definitely good, waiter is kind and caring. Besides, the waiter will also recommend to you what's more popular and also what to order if you so wish it.Food, I had ordered a Parisian Hot Chocolate, Antipasti Salad, Mushroom Soup, Squid Ink Pasta, Pork Rib Eye, Pork Loin Chop, and a Wagyu Striploin steak.First of all, the Antipasti Salad is good with an assortment of vegetables (one has a hint of mint to it), bacon, cheese, and longan, which gives it a refreshing taste plus a rich body of taste.Next is the mushroom soup, I must say, it tastes wonderful. Perhaps I have not tasted much mushroom soups, but it is one of the best that I have tried. It has a rich mushroom smell and taste and it is very creamy. One of the thing that it did right is the mushroom is pureed well, it doesn't have the coarse texture that you might find in many places that cooked the same style of mushroom soup. The only flaw is that the bread that comes with the soup is not up to par as it taste really basic, not one you would expect in this kind of restaurant.Now, about the Pork Rib Eye and Pork Loin Chop, I must say that I'm very disappointed with what they served me. I heard that they uses the slow cook method such that the pork chop will be tender and juicy inside and a slight grill after that to give the surface and nice color and texture. However, I found that the inside is not tender at all, giving me a very bad experience. You can go to Ante to try out their pork chop, it is in One Utama as well and their pork chop is what I would a call a slow cooked pork chop done right.Next comes the Wagyu Striploin steak, which is kind of disappointing for me as well. If it is only about the wellness of the steak, it is done right. However, there's a burnt taste on the steak that is rather unpalatable, it had gone over from a wonderful charred taste to an unacceptable burnt taste. Other than that, the supposedly "Wagyu" is not tasty at all. I've tasted an authentic A5 grade Kobe Wagyu steak in Japan before, and of course, I'm not expecting them to provide me something of equal quality given the price tag, however, I would still expect a steak that is more tender, with decent marbling, and a decent beef fragrant, but all that I can tell is that the beef is juicier than a normal beef by a small margin with no noticable better beef fragrant at all. To be honest, I would pay anything more than RM 60 for a steak like this.Squid Ink Pasta, I'm a little bit disappointed by this dish as well. To be honest, the only thing that is good about this dish is the fresh prawn and spaghetti cooked to al dente. Taste wise, it is a very simple taste, something akin to aglio olio, however, it tasted too oily for me.All in all, the only reason that I'm giving 2 stars rather than less is due to the good service, good mushroom soup, and good ambience. If I factor in the price tag and, at least the dishes that I have tried today, 2 stars is really what it deserves in my opinion.
Location: Lot G146, Ground Floor (Old Wing), 1Utama Shopping Centre, 47800 PJ, Selangor, Malaysia, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Probably one of the best Thai street food that I've eaten so far!When a group of foodies sat down and talked, the conversation revolved around on …MoreProbably one of the best Thai street food that I've eaten so far!When a group of foodies sat down and talked, the conversation revolved around on where to eat, what's best and what's not, etc... the conversation led to Thai food and I remember one of them mentioned about Jatujak in Ara Damansara. So one fine day, I picked up a good friend who loves his food as much as his wines.It seemed that he was in the mood for some Thai fares, and quickly pointed me to where Jatujak was - it's my favourite Thai restaurant, he said! Since there were only two of us, we couldn't order a lot.◾Thai-style steamed siakap & clam - it took only a spoonful to convince me that they mean business. The flavour was very balanced in between spicy and soury. If you ask me, I don't really like the meat texture of siakap but he was buying lunch so I makan je la. I couldn't stop drinking the soup and sweating at the same time 😅◾stir fried pucuk paku - crunchy and fresh with a tinge of spiciness.◾Khao Kha Moo aka Thai slow braised pork knuckle - I was in the mood for pork and this didn't disappoint. Packed with flavour from the gravy with soft & tender meat, plus the green for the crunchiness and egg for extra protein.◾coconut ice cream - didn't expect much but I was wowed by the ice cream. Not too sweet with distinctive coconut taste.A permanent fixture in my Thai food list now.
Location: 23, Jalan PJU 1a/3j, Ara Damansara, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Anastasia Soh
Review: “Probably The Best Thai Food In Town”Overall: Having spent a year in Thailand, we grew to love both the Thai culture …More“Probably The Best Thai Food In Town”Overall: Having spent a year in Thailand, we grew to love both the Thai culture & the delicious food. Whilst we were in Malaysia, we have been on a hunt for delicious and authentic Thai food but have yet to find one. With their bold promise of “probably being the best thai food in town”, we transport you back to the days where we could still dine-in to discover if this Thai Restaurant is able to deliver.Phad Thai RM (14.90)Ask any Thai. Phad Thai is never complete without supplementary fish sauce & additional sugar readily available. Today, despite not being provided, the dish in itself was delicious enough. It was not too dry, slightly moist with a hint of sweet. Just the way it is usually cooked in Thailand & absolutely delicious! Therefore even if they did provide fish sauce & sugar, we probably won’t have used it anyway.Seafood Curry Powder (RM 45)Taste: A perfect melody of fresh seafood fried to perfection in an extremely flavourful curry. We could smell the dish even before it arrived at our table which made our mouths water.Mince Pork Omelette (RM 19)What sets Thai omelette apart from others is the fluffiness & crispiness of it resulting from running it through a strainer & into boiling hot oil. Though the omelette was flavourful & crispy, it wasn’t as fluffy as we would have liked it to be.All in all, despite its shortfalls, it was still delicious but could have been slightly better. It is not probably the best. It is, THE BEST we have had thus far. Judging from the quality of the food, we are willing to bet that the chefs that made the magic happen are actually Thai.Our full review is on Instagram (@monk3yseendo)
Location: 23, Jalan PJU 1a/3j, Ara Damansara, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

The description in the menu stated that it’s a traditional home style hearty fried rice with cabbage, braised meat, baby shrimps, mushrooms, clams and scallops BUT in reality there were barely any ingredients in it!! No seafood or braised meat like what was stated in the menu 😤 Extremely misleading and disappointing! Thankfully the pillowy, golden fried sesame bun filled with stir-fried shredded lean pork for savoury burst of flavours in every bite was a delight 🐷❤️ I will give them a benefit of doubt as I dined alone that day and couldn’t order much of their signatures. I assume I didn’t order the right dishes, so I might give them a second chance 🙄

Review: We have been going to this place since 2014. I must say, their portions have shrunk substantially and this has affected the standard in their food. We were there last week, and noticed that a few tapas were not as good as they used to be. …MoreWe have been going to this place since 2014. I must say, their portions have shrunk substantially and this has affected the standard in their food. We were there last week, and noticed that a few tapas were not as good as they used to be. For example, their baked mushrooms have shrunk and this in turn affected the texture of the dish. The mushrooms now look wrinkled and pathetic. To add insult to injury, their Spanish croquettes used to be very good. But now, they have reduced the size of these croquettes so much that one can no longer taste the creaminess of the fillings and can only taste the breadcrumbs coating of the croquettes. The whole thing tasted dry. For their Gambas al ajillo (garlic prawns), although the size of their prawns is still the same but I noticed that they now give you 6 prawns instead of 8. In the past, they were quite generous with the garlic bits in this dish (hello, it's called garlic prawns for a reason!), it has now reduced by at least 60%! I understand that times are tough with Covid-19, but I hope the operators can continue to maintain the standard in their food. After all, they did revise their prices not too long ago.From a concerned loyal customer.

Review: Haven't had such a unique gastronomical experience like this before, and Kayra delivers it well. No wonder why it was listed as one of the top 20 restaurants on Tatler Dining list in 2021. No wonder why it was listed as one of the top 20 restaurants on Tatler Dining list in 2021. Well-deserved!It's worth a try for those looking for authentic Kerala cuisines and would like to try something other than banana leaf rice (Indian food isn't just about banana leaf rice by the way 😆). Their sea bass is tender and fresh, while their dosa taco is a unique take on the traditional tacos! As Chinese, I've always had our claypot chicken rice growing up and never tasted the Indian version of it, and it didn't disappoint. It's extremely different from Chinese claypot rice as this one is coated with curry and various types of veggies.Their beverage menu is quite interesting too, but I was less adventurous and only went with Mango Lassi, which is rich and creamy, and it met my expectations.Overall Kayra was an eye-opener to me. Will absolutely bring any food adventurer here for a celebration. Keep it up, Kayra!

Review: a'Roma Dinings opened its door in Paramount Garden, an older part of PJ and since then.. have quietly yet surely established themselves as the mainstay Italian restaurant in this area. During MCO, they practice close adherents to the SOP.◾Complimentary crispy cracker-like bread with tomato based dipping sauce.◾Tagliere di Salumi E Formaggi - 4 different types of cold cuts & artisanal cheese with accompaniment. Nothing beats cold cuts, cheese and red wine pairing.◾Costolette Di Agnello - whole rack of lamb served with red wine reduction sauce, spinach, German potato. The lamb racks were done perfectly as ordered (medium) with all the sides arranged neatly on the side. The red wine reduction sauce went very very well with the lamb rack, and the Barolo that I drank somehow enhanced in flavour when I drank it after each bite.◾Spaghetti Alma Carbonara Con Pancetta which comprises of spaghettini, kampung egg, home cured Pancetta, pecorino and Grana Padano... the texture was al dente and the Carbonara sauce tasted original and not pretentious at all. I am sure that even the small ones will find this hard to resist if placed in front of them.◾homemade sausage with grilled vegetables - the best way to enjoy sausages and not to worry about any preservative.◾ special pasta (seasonal menu) - I didn't get to taste this as it was my customer's but he did mention that the texture was good and he slurped up everything on the plate including the sauce.Based on my dining experience, I reckon that this restaurant is going to be here for the long term, that is, if MCO didn't cause substantial damage to the operation. I pray that they will survive this so I can come back again with the family in the future.Armed with a beautiful Aussie Chardonnay and then followed by an excellent Barolo before completed by a 25 years old Japanese whisky.. I would say that the whole dining experience was a great one!

With yellow painted wall and ample lighting, it is cosy and inviting.  There is also a wine counter.We had deep fried chicken spring rolls (MYR22), vegetarian claypot (MYR28) and deep fried eggplant (MYR18),  For drinks, I ordered the pina colada (MYR27) and wife had the lime juice with ginger (MYR15).  A very simple and authentic Vietnamese meal which we enjoyed very much.The spring rolls were deeply fried and came with lot of herbs and greeny salad.  Wrap with mint leave and dip in the sweet sauce, it is simply delicious.Instead of having too much meat, we went for the vegetarian claypot.  Ingredients included tofu, carrot, spring onion and mushroom over steamed white rice.  A nice change.Eggplant was soft and a little oily.  The skin was too hard to consume.  I believe you will just skip the skin.The pina colada was a concoction of pineapple juice, rum and coconut milk.  I could taste the strong flavour of coconut.  Nice.  Lime juice with ginger has a very strong taste of ginger.If you like authentic Vietnamese food, this may a right restaurant in the Changkat Bintang area.  Service is good. Additionally, you get the same piping hot fried there and then fried stuffs. Notably, I only noticed fish and chicken though. We picked up our choices of dishes, which we self scoop over the plate of rice.Returning back to our table in this rather plain and simple ambiance, we  decided to top up. A plate of mutton varuval/dry style and chicken parathal/dry style. Anyway, let me tell you. There's really not much of a difference between Asian Rice Pot and other similar Indian eateries. Nothing much, honestly, I didn't notice any unique or different dishes. We had also called for our drinks and these had already arrived by the we tucked into our meal.What's my say on Asian Rice Pot? Mutton Parathal fared quiet okay. Soft tender easily chewable meat in a tasty thick spicy gravy/curry, cooked alongside the customary spices and chillies. However, it lacked the spicy kick I am accustomed to. Even my friends agreed with me. Thank god. The Chicken varuval, another common fare was a decent dish though I won't give it a hype. Basically, just ordinary. The rest of the side items we tucked into were decently elevated too.Now, lemme tell you about the drinks. Thick, creamy and slushy Mango Lassi did wonder on my tongue. Love it. Pure and authentic. Lemongrass Lemon Ice was praise by my friend. Then again, what can go wrong as long you get to taste the citrusy and lemony infuses. Tea Tarik of course was appreciated. Always will be after a spicy Indian meal. This not overly sweet tea must be credited.Was it worth me coming over all the way from Shah Alam. Sincerely, I could have had such a meal somewhere close by my area. Even so, I'll take this food venture as my blogging experience. That's it. Wonder why my friends had to speak highly about Asian Rice Pot? Because of the owner and their close friendship? You figure out.

Review: Hands up, how many of you have passed by centerstage but never knew what was inside? Wait do you even know where centerstage is? …MoreHands up, how many of you have passed by centerstage but never knew what was inside? Wait do you even know where centerstage is?On the table today is Calamari Fritti (RM26.90), Tagliatelle Al Prosciutto (RM42.63) and 11" La Pizza Swirl (RM48.25).I thought I ordered too much but visually they look like small plates. Let's start with the calamari, as an Italian restaurant, you cannot afford to screw this dish up. The dish is nice, batter good and both the dips nice.Next is the tagliatelle, if you have not tried parma ham then once in your life you should. This dish, I'm on the fence because the base tasted like cream of chicken. The parma ham is cured and salty; so there is really no need for the base broth. In the end, when you dig in , you will get pockets of saltiness.Lastly, the pizza swirl looks small but it will pack a punch. The mozzarella cheese is chewy which I like but there is something that lets this down. The thing with dough is that you never know it's is thoroughly cooked when it's curled up. So the outer sides are crispy and the insides are crispy but the middle feels uncooked so there is feeling of biting into thick flaky dough. Not cool. Otherwise this was a novel way of eating pizza.Overall the environment is not welcoming, that's because it's located in a mall that is not doing well. It feels run down and I think it has affected the overall morale of the servers and also chefs. Imagine working at a place where left, right and center is all up for rent and sale. Happy workers is as important as good food.*NOTE* This is not a paid post; the written content is based on author's personal opinion and preference.For more food reviews, follow me on IG at @seniorglutton

The sauce didn't help either cause it was like what you get out of a packet from the supermarket. The short grain butter rice served together with it felt out of place too. As for the other dishes, the Puttanesca sauce provided with the Fried Calamari was good and the Tiramisu was well made.The dining experience here was sort of a mixed bag. Great service but just normal tasting food as personally I view the Enormous Pizzas with "unique" flavours merely gimmicky (e.g. Carbonara Pizza). With that said, maybe this place is just really for fans of ridiculously large Pizzas.

Review: We brought the Goh family (no, not the Medici family of Florence of Renaissance Italy!) to Fellini for Boxing Day lunch and everyone was completely Sated & Satisfied (my 2 ‘S’) at the end of the meal, harbouring no post-prandial regrets at …MoreWe brought the Goh family (no, not the Medici family of Florence of Renaissance Italy!) to Fellini for Boxing Day lunch and everyone was completely Sated & Satisfied (my 2 ‘S’) at the end of the meal, harbouring no post-prandial regrets at all! Unlike some other restaurants in the Klang Valley which sell food that passes off as Italian but is actually ersatz, this is the real Mc Coy! The antipasto platters of salami and other cured meats plus herbs, cheeses etc.drizzled with olive oil were enjoyable. These were complemented by platters of slices of crusty bread and toppings of pate di funghi. Sublime! Then came plates of mixed seafood spaghetti and two more with sauce carbonara. But to meat lovers like us, the piece de resistance were definitely the roasted lamb shanks that followed the pasta dishes! Tender pieces of meat that literally detached themselves from the bone with little effort. Needless to say, no sooner the phrase “buon appetito” were uttered than within minutes, the shanks disappeared quickly into our alimentary tracts to placate our porcine appetites! Rounding up the meals, maestro chef & owner, Tony — who hails from Rome and who specially curated the meal for us — indulged us with his ambrosial home made Gelato, Tiramisu and ice cream! It would be superfluous to say that our Boxing Day lunch at Fellini today was a memorable gastronomic experience that composer-cum-gastronome, Rossini himself, would have given thumbs up! My only cavil here is that I wish they would use Aceto Basalmico of Modena for the dips and also the absence in the menu of Cianghiale alla Cacciatora (and has to be only the wild boar of Tuscany, fed with the chestnuts found there!). But that would have added extra cost to the meal, which on the whole was reasonable, to state the least. And after such a good meal like this, one comes to the conclusion that few can repudiate the assertion of the denizens of Italy when they claim that only they know what “the sweet life” is all about, the phrase as encapsulated in the title of a film of one of Italy’s famous directors, Federico Fellini (who also happens to be Tony’s favourite one, hence the name of his restaurant in Petaling Jaya): La Dolce Vita!
Location: 119, Jalan Gasing, Pjs 10, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

It reminded me of my favourite nasi lemak curry chicken that my mom used to tapau. Sadly, that stall no longer exist.The fish gulai assam was excellent too. It was really fresh and the assam curry broth hit all the right notes.We also had paku pakis, which was fresh and really good.Finally, the rum and raisins ice cream, came with generous portion of rum and well made ice cream which wasn't too sweet.Price: Slightly Pricier (about 130 for the four of us)Food: ExcellentWill I return: definitelyBrotip:1) Book your seats early as some days they have to turn people away.2) Order the nasi briyani and beef rendang in advance. Review: An old school, not quite fine dining establishment, Sri Nyonya delivers what it promises; high quality nyonya food but at high prices. …MoreAn old school, not quite fine dining establishment, Sri Nyonya delivers what it promises; high quality nyonya food but at high prices.Sri Nyonya is in a word, nostalgic. The restaurant itself is heavily decorated in Baba Nyonya style albeit, one that is situated in Petaling Jaya. The rattan chairs are comfortable though old and could use lumbar support. The table cloths are soft pink; unusual since I don't think the color has much effect compared to yellow or blue. But nothing is uncomfortable and all seems to be in it's place. The space is small but able to accommodate 40 to 50 pax at a time.And the food is high quality due to them using fresh - really fresh - ingredients. The Nyonya Fried Rice is just a typical fried rice but the carrots and green onions were bright and vibrant with no signs of oxidation. The prawns still tasted of the sea; amazing since we are nowhere near the sea. The Chicken Rendang had a good balance of salty, sweet, sour and spicy without one overpowering another. The kerisik had a caramelly taste and the gravy was smooth without feeling grainy.What holds Sri Nyonya back though, is the price. You will be forgiven to have doubts about spending RM16 for a plate fried rice and RM23 for a serving of Chicken Rendang, on top of which, you are also charged 10% service charge. Sri Nyonya is definitely not for college students and not even for most white collar class, which is perhaps the reason why there were so many senior citizens dining.If money is no issue, Sri Nyonya is recommended for great Nyonya food in Petaling Jaya.
Location: 14, Jalan 22/49, Seksyen 22, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Not to forget to their hand-cut fried chips, those are so lovely, thumbs up as it would let you forget about those commercial potato chips!Dinner menu:1. A warm, hearty, rich, filling, and silky smooth, creamy mushroom soup. The earthy flavours of mushrooms at its best pureéd into this soup along with sourdough toast. The Mushroom Medley Soup with Sourdough toast.2. A combination of soft brie, curd springy mozzarella, gritty parmesan, light and glorious ricotta in one pizza with porcini mushroom puree, rosemary, and muscatel (type of wine made of muscat grapes). Top pick for cheese lovers. Experience the bursting flavours in one bite.3. A just nice crust, not too thin or thick. Rustic edge, crispy with some chewiness dough in the middle. Perfectly served with its seafood fiesta with crab meat, prawn, mussel, squid on the authentic tomato based sauce, topped with oregano, mozzarella, and parmesan. Mild-sweet white flakes, firm yet tender halibut fish wrapped in golden and super crispy batter one and only by Botanica+Co, Halibut Fish & Chips with bunch of steak fries underneath, tartar sauce and a bowl of refreshing vinaigrette salads on the side. Everything compliments each others. My best-pick dish of Botanica+Co for its worthy price.5. In the other hand, Botanica+Co brilliantly came out with this dessert called Churros Doughnut Stack, which a tower of guilty pleasure! It has crunchy exterior which resembles churros while inside is soft and moist like Doughnut. Then it leaves ice cream surprise inside which is protected in the ring, covered with torched-whipped cream and drizzled with caramel and chocolate.6. Presented as a familiar dish of apple crumble, this is a playful twist which came out as banana crumble. Structured from baked caramelised banana on the bottom to crumb mixture, topped with fresh seasonal fruits, sprinkled powdered sugar, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. A perfect combination of hot and cold desserts such a great dessert on this season, ensuing a gleeful season!

Author: Nick Au
Review: I think I am being rather generous with 2 star review. There was one redeeming moment but the rest was not that great. …MoreI think I am being rather generous with 2 star review. There was one redeeming moment but the rest was not that great.The place is rather new to most of us, hence I've decided to jump the bandwagon to give it a try. Came by on 29/5/17 around 8.30pm and walked in thru the front door. There were two tables occupied on the ground floor, saw a lady in a 3 pax table waiving at the waiter, he came to me instead and sat me down. Lady was still waving as the waiter asked me of I'd be fine with the bar counter and I was. Had a tap on my shoulder and lo and behold my friends were on their date night and said hello. All this time, lady was still waving, so I gave the lady's hand a break and decided to point it out to the waiter that someone's asking for service. Off he went and I took a seat. Looked around for a minute or two, wait staffs zipping by and no one came to give me a menu. Then I realised, it's on the countertop leaning against the wall. I guess it's a casual joint so I've perused thru the menu.Took another look around and no one came by to take my order or start me off with a drink or even explain what's the menu about. I mean I'm dying to be sold the place but zilch. I decided to take matters in my own hands and waves to one of the waiter who is quite tall. He sees me, and rushes over so I'm all settled to make an order but he zips past and picks the house phone. Odd I thought he did see me. Once he's done I tried to tell him I'd like to place an order, he zips past me again to the door to assist a 2 pax to their table. There was another waiter already assisting the 2 pax with their enquiry. I waved at the waiter once again and again was ignored whilst he was watching the enquiries being handled by his colleague.I literally had to stare him in the eye as he walks past by and ask if I could place an order. To which he finally obliged. Ordered a pizza and root beer. The root beer came by, it was flat. I asked to change the root beer because it came poured out into a glass (didn't know it was cans), the waitress tells me "It's flat? But we just pour it out from the can.". And no offers of changing it or suggestong something else. By the way, I think your suppliers are giving you a bad supply of root beer, it's so flat even when I whisk my straw around to show the waitress, there wasn't any bubbles.The food came, now onto the pizza. By Malaysian standard it is much better than a lot of places I've been to. Which is good but man, the dough is chewy and toothsome. The crust bottom tastes of burnt charcoal. The dough has no flavour whatsoever. It could have been a piece of cardboard and may have just worked the same. The toppings good though. Generous with cheese, chorizo and tomatoes. The tomatoes are also sliced thick and I can tastes the freshness. That's good.So where's the redeeming quality? Remember my friends that's on their date night? Well they ordered a truffle pizza, and wanted to share a slice so I said sure. Whilst they were cutting a slice for me, I was awkwardly holding onto to a side plate. One of the waiter saw it and came to help to pass the plate. Good for you.There was another incident whereby they wanted to ask me if I wanted to move from the bar to one of the smaller tables. It was a good intention, but the phrasing was not quite delicate. Waitress came to me and ask "Do you mind moving to the small table?" Review: I've never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has offered better service and hospitality than Curate, Four Seasons. I went to the restaurant to celebrate my mother's birthday and I was not disappointed. …MoreI've never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has offered better service and hospitality than Curate, Four Seasons. I went to the restaurant to celebrate my mother's birthday and I was not disappointed.The atmosphere is what you can expect out of a five star hotel. Curate will make you feel like you're in the shoes of a millionaire for a day. Marble floors, art decors that span a dining table for twelve, and warm tones reflected off the lighting. There's that perfect amount of space to explore what the restaurant has to offer without feeling like you're going to bump into someone's table. It's luxurious but you don't feel ostracized or out of place.At the time, the buffet was split into a small selection of regional dishes. Local, Middle Eastern, and Italian. There's dessert, a cheese platter, a salad bar and a selection of juices. That was it. However, all of them were immaculately presented and they tasted amazing. The texture of the beef rendang, the hummus, the lamb, was on point. There was nothing up for offer that wasn't a burst of flavors. Quality over quantity. Every meal was fresh to the taste and warm to the touch.The service was the main feature to write home about. The waiters and waitresses were always attentive. They made sure that our plates were replaced once we were done eating and that our glasses were never empty. While I was browsing through the buffet, Chef Qal introduced himself to me and asked me how the food was. He was heartwarmingly friendly and we got along well. He told me the process the Curate staff goes through to ensure the food's freshness and how the restaurant determines what dishes they would like to put on display. It was an insightful experience made even better when he arbitrarily planned out a celebration the moment he heard that I was here to celebrate my mother's birthday. On the house, Chef Qal ensured that their customers were having the best experience was the restaurant's top priority.I say it again because I cannot stress it enough. I have never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has given me and my family this amount of love, friendliness and hospitality. I recommend this restaurant to everyone.
Location: 145, Jln Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Tanski
Review: Am making my evaluation by comparing to KL fine dining restaurants of similar standards ie lunch @RM350+ per pax. …MoreAm making my evaluation by comparing to KL fine dining restaurants of similar standards ie lunch @RM350+ per pax.What’s good:1. Reservation. Quick. Responsive.2. Nice ambience. Clean. Modern. Good first impression. Good potential.What needs improvements:1. Poor table setting. Disbelief is the word in their cutleries selection for such an establishment. Only provided 1 set of cutlery for entree, starter and main course. I felt like I was lunching in a hall.  When the main dish turned up, I had to use my used “butter knife” for my beef dish. And….cheap thin paper napkins!  Really! Seriously!  😱 This must be the 1st thing that I will want changed.2. Service. Forgettable. Un-attentive. Didn’t fill empty glasses. Impersonal. When they explained a dish, they did not engage with customers. It’s just doing their job - repeat the standard line, drop the dish and go. Next. Can’t say they are not efficient 🤭.3. Feeding session.  There was no pacing at all.  From bread, to amuse bouche, to starter to soup to main. Immediately follow by dessert and petit fours. Not more than 5 minutes in between.  I cannot fathom why they served dessert and petit fours together….and the waiter told us to eat the petit fours first, becoz the sorbet was melting.  Meanwhile, the truffle ice cream on my chestnut dessert was already half melted when it arrived on my table. 😧3. Amuse Bouche. When food arrived on the table, its already cold. You can it has sitting out for a bit.  Tanjong Malim “Caviar” was interesting, but the “char kuih” it was served on was oily.  Chicken cordon bleu was wrapped with 2 small pieces of toast, I thought was not necessary. The toast was soft, not toasty when served to us. The chicken was cold and the cheese was already hard.  I left the toast and the “char kuih” on the plate.  Probably it’s the New Year Day lunch menu and prepared ahead….but no excuses for them given the price they are asking. Oh, the amuse bouche was supposed to be eaten with fingers, but there were no wet wipes provided. 🙄4. Entree & Soup.  Salmon tartare was decent, delicate tasting similar to Sashimi. Pretty plating, nothing special though. Lacked acids.  The abalone truffle soup was a let down. Could have done without the foie gras, it was just  too overpowering for the delicate soup. Soup was also clunky as the root vegetables were cut too large, and could be cooked longer. The soup came with a big pastry that I thought was just unnecessary.  It just fills you up with no additional taste. More carbs again after “char kuih” and toast in Amuse Bouche.  You are a fine dining restaurant, not a bistro…so size doesn’t matter. 🤔5. Main.  Beef with truffle sauce.  Liked the delicate clean presentation of the beef and the potato mille feuille. Enjoyed that. Would be even better if the dish was served warmer, as the potato was on the cool side and I didn’t get the taste texture it intended.  Slightly chewy.6. Dessert & Petit Fours. The dessert came with great presentation and original taste. I was impressed. But when served together with Petit Fours…….it got lost. (Item 3. above).  One of the petit fours was a piece of nougat….sticky and sweet. Definitely not for picking it up with fingers, as it sticks like glue when it starts to melt.  I think it can do with a thin piece of wafer.7. Coffee or Tea.  None. Waiter cleared our table, and didn’t offer any coffee or tea. For RM350 per pax, I would have thought they would at least ask if we had wanted any…...we didnt mind paying for the coffee if it wasn’t included in the price.  But since they didn’t ask, I didn’t bother either.  I just asked for the bill. 🧐In Summary:Definitely below expectations when compared to other similar tier fine dining restaurants. Food was presented well (like others of the same class), taste was ok (like the others), nothing that ‘delight’ the pallet.  Service and the overall experience was the main give away.  Will I go back again….guess will have to wait a long while, may be until I forget this “forgettable” experience. 🙃

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Value for money French fine-diningThere's a reason why Entier is always booked out for their lunch sessions - good …MoreValue for money French fine-diningThere's a reason why Entier is always booked out for their lunch sessions - good food with affordable pricing. And I only found out about this when she directed me to the obscure part of Brickfields where Alila Bangsar (technically the building is in Brickfields area but with a connecting bridge to Bangsar LRT station)."Atceli I tried to book for many weeks already but it was always fully-booked" she said. My heart melted when I got to know how she went through the hassle to surprise me, as I know the fact that she isn't very much a planner herself. Located on the 41st floor, we got ourselves a table by the window overseeing Brickfields and beyond.I kepoh a bit and took a look around - the restaurant was definitely full house and everyone was seen enjoying their lunch over chatters. Complimentary bread with kombu butter (which was heavenly by the way) was served as soon as we placed our order. I had to order a second kombu butter because it was so good.So there are two (2) options: 2-Course (RM108) without dessert or 3-Course Lunch Set (RM128) with dessert.Starters◾ Garlic & Escargot Soup - garlic veloute (soup); vegetable stock; escargot beignet; garlic croutons. So the escargot was deep fried with greenish colour dough on the outside and served on the plate which covered the bowl of soup. The idea was to pour everything into the soup and enjoyed like that.◾Salmon & Katsuo - cured Norwegian salmon tartare, nage of Katsuo, kombu dashi, salmon roe. Delicious but I could not help but to think that it tasted more Japanese than French.Mains◾Duck & Potato - duck confit Parmentier, mushroom, mashed potato and crispy tuile. I was impressed by the presentation of the dish. All elements combined well together to make my tummy happy.◾Butter Fish - butter fish beignet; sauteed pea sprout; mashed potato; pickled pearl onion. I took a bite and still prefer my duck dish. Given the choice, I'd normally go for red meat as main. The pickled onion did its job to cut through the richness of the sauce.Desserts◾Banana Éclair - banana eclair; 70% single Pahang chocolate cream, yoghurt ice cream. I wouldn't order banana dessert if not for the other half who wanted to try it. Lovely dessert which was not too sweet yet got me wanted for more.Each set comes with complimentary tea/coffee or homemade kombucha (soda).Lunch Hour Wine Specials @ RM60 nett for any 2 glasses of white (Italian verdicchio), red (negroamaro) or pink sparkling (rose brut).Lunch was good, the companion was beautiful and most importantly, we left the restaurant satisfied with the overall food quality and service. Now she wants to come back for dinner already.
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Anastasia Soh
Review: Pushing Home Fine-Dining To The Limits  First off, this is a review of their food delivery and not dine-in  Service: The order was placed via their friendly operator on WhatsApp who gave pretty good recommendations  Packaging: Though the …MorePushing Home Fine-Dining To The Limits  First off, this is a review of their food delivery and not dine-in  Service: The order was placed via their friendly operator on WhatsApp who gave pretty good recommendations  Packaging: Though the packaging wasn’t fancy but we loved the little branding finishes especially the jams and butters. More impressively, the plating was able to survive the delivery  Entier 3 Course Meal (RM 98)  Taste: In an attempt to satisfy our craving for French food, we chanced upon the very reasonably priced 3 course meal offered by Entier with their nose to tail philosophy. Each set is accompanied by a freshly baked home-made corn bread, kombu butter & a strawberry & lavender jam. Nothing we enjoyed more than the delightful crunch as we broke into the crusty yet fluffy bread with our eyes closed, savouring the moment.  Our prawn and mango starter gave us a refreshing start to the meal with a touch of sweet and fruitiness from the mango chutney which went beautifully with the vadouvan oil giving it a slightly spiced and curried flavour. This was jam-packed with garden fresh herbs in a wonton looking pouch which excited diners are able to burst spilling the precious contents within.  Our Cured Scottish salmon was fresh and cooked perfectly with a beautiful tinge of pink rested on spring beans and sautéed spinach which gave the dish an exciting crunch completed with a zesty lemon butter sauce.  Completing the meal was a beautifully glazed hazelnut eclair filled with sea salt caramel and hazelnut cream which provided an amazing balance of sweet and salty.Entier has pushed home fine-dining both presentation and flavours to the very limits  Our full review is on Instagram (@monk3yseendo)
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

Author: CY Liew
Review: I am a returning customer at Entier.Pros: Food as usual, was good. …MoreI am a returning customer at Entier.Pros: Food as usual, was good.Cons:-	What I have observed since my first visit and was unchanged was the service. For a fine-dining restaurant, I would have expected better service (i.e., more attentive to customers, refill the drinks without needing to be requested twice, be gentler in serving and collecting). I noticed not all waiters were trained to par. On my first visit, the waiter did not seem happy doing his job. On my return visit, the gentleman who served me was no different and additionally, did not ask about what I thought of my food and did not do more than only serving (no explanation of the platters), in addition to not doing the duties mentioned earlier.-	I was very unhappy that Entier cancelled my reservation after the confirmation call made the night before my noon reservation. I was busy and could not attend to the calls. When I called back, the staff mentioned that they called the wrong number and the customer cancelled the reservation, although I did receive 2 miss calls earlier. I will leave this to your own interpretation.I would recommend that – 1. Collect a reservation deposit to ensure a lower percentage of last-minute cancellation; 2. Make the reservation confirmation call at least 24 hours prior; 3. Do not cancel a reservation before the customer gets the chance call back after the missed call. Hence, point no.1&2.-	In terms of cleanliness, the table and couch were not properly cleaned. Small pieces of food were found in between the couch. This made me doubt that the area was properly cleaned, let alone sanitized thoroughly as required during this pandemic.I would love to visit again as I loved the ambience and food. However, based on my experience on my second visit, I will not be returning. This is not service expected for a restaurant of this tier. Disappointed.
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Viktor Tey
Review: Located on the 41st floor of Tower Alila Bangsar, Entier is a semi-hidden gem of gastronomy. …MoreLocated on the 41st floor of Tower Alila Bangsar, Entier is a semi-hidden gem of gastronomy.The transition from the outdoor valet parking, through the double doors and elevator to the grand reception of the Alila hotel is seamless, yet jarring. The scale of it all as you enter the naturally lit,  wood and stone lobby invites you into a new world, a castle in the sky.Walking in to the restaurant was another memorable moment as we passed by the indoor swimming pool. We were seated promptly and were one of the first tables there. We were unable to secure a seat with a view, but it was to our relief that the glass walls permitted us to see as freely as we wanted.The staff of Entier are united in their courtesy and helpfulness. With their suggestion, we went for the 2pax tasting menu. Suffice to say our palates were satisfied with the results.Even as the night went on, the ambiance in the restaurant shifts to a dimmer, more romantic setting. It was unfortunate that the sunset is not visible (as it was on the other side of the building).The wine pairings with the menu were distinct from one another, and play a wonderful supporting role to the dishes of the night, which centered around the theme of seafood.There was plenty of caviar on our menu, (perhaps a little too much), and it certainly felt extravagant and worth the expense. Overall though, our aim was to enjoy the atmosphere and dining experience. It was unfortunate that there was a large party with children celebrating next to us, which offered some distraction to our night. But my good natured date and I took it in stride, given it was our first fine dining experience we had no prior expectations to meet.In summary, I would say that a visit to Entier is worthwhile especially for a romantic night out, but do book your tables early to avoid disappointment. We would return again someday hopefully to celebrate our 5th year together.Entier French Dining is recommended.
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

Review: If there is an option to have 0 stars, I would have chosen that option.My recent experience was only 3 days ago, that Entier left me utterly …MoreIf there is an option to have 0 stars, I would have chosen that option.My recent experience was only 3 days ago, that Entier left me utterly disappointed.The summary is as below:1. Poor coordination of dish delivery. All appetisers were served in one go. We had preordered 6 appetisers and all came out at the same time. The restaurant is most probably under staffed as well whereby the waiters did not have time to even explain us the food while serving us the dishes.2. Main courses ordered, approx 1kg cōte de boeuf, whole duck and saddle (approx 1kg of lamb). These orders were made in advance so that they could prepare them for a special dinner we planned for my family. However, it ended up with a disastrous dinner experience.All of the meat were served out at once and that shocked us with a scene that we were expected to eat all 3 different kind of meats at one go. I wonder which chef of a certain standard would do so to their customers without telling them in advance that it would be his / her way of presenting their dishes? It was literally almost similar to food at a food court where all food was served at once.3. Hygiene sensitivity. During the current pandemic, it would have been better to be more vigilant of the hygiene of the food. Our situation was a guest from another table came by without wearing face mask and keep taking photos of the meats that were presented to us. He took photos at such a close distance that his face was close by and sleeves was so close to our food that we wouldn’t be comfortable to even dig in if we were to continue the meal. Not to mention, the guest even pushed away my sister as if that it was his order. This all happened when I was complaining to the waiter that it is unacceptable to have food served all at once, and the waiter didn’t even know what to do.4. Service of restaurant manager. It took him quite some time to approach us. We even observed that he was standing from far seeing the whole situation unfold and didn’t even take the initiative to step up. Well, after 5-10 minutes or so, finally he came. We gave him all the feedback and situation, and could even report this restaurant to the authorities on its unhygienic practices (letting other guests to smell your food while it’s being presented), he did nothing and said that he will keep the other two meats and would serve in sequence after while he replace the duck due to the other guest’s action. He then diverted everything to the chef since he couldn’t do anything except for saying they will take our feedback and allow them to improve. Unfortunately, not even my phone number that was requested and instead he gave me his name card. I’m sorry, it’s like you have a bad service, customers have to give you the chance, customer have to contact you after? Doesn’t make sense at all. It was just pure low level and poor quality public relations to push away a customer.4. The head chef. There’s no need to mention the name as his name is all over Entier’s introduction in their website. We asked for him to come explain to us the rationality of the issue but to our upmost disappointment, knowing Japanese chef’s they respect they would stand up to the problem. Pure Japanese practical approach. However, what we saw was, he came by the glass from the outside, look at us, then walked in. Up to you reviewers to judge yourself on this.Lastly, we were so disappointed with the service and food, and asked for the bill specifically asking them to charge everything to our bill because it would be paying for a bad experience and we that will never come again. Nevertheless, they did take away the 3 main courses from the bill and gave a 10% service discount, and they insisted not to charge us.So far, only an automatic generated feedback sent to the email we provided during the reservation, and no effort for this restaurant to improve.Another restaurant gone into no go list in KL.

Author: Solarance Shiro
Review: Went with my boyfriend’s family for the first time trying out the food here.. I’ll explain the food that I ate though since it’s only fair 😂 …MoreWent with my boyfriend’s family for the first time trying out the food here.. I’ll explain the food that I ate though since it’s only fair 😂1. I had the vegetable soup 🍲 and it tasted like creamy pumpkin with corn and it has a hint of truffle oil taste in it... it was quite sweet but good enough to keep on eating without feeling much sickness 😂 (I had lactose intolerance).2. I had the venison (Medium rare) and it’s served with pumpkin and beetroot purée. Honestly, the sauce is a bit salty but with the pumpkin purée which is just the right amount of sweetness to help balance the flavours of the dish overall. The meat is tender and pink on the inside and was flavoured perfectly.3. The dessert, we ordered the soufflé and the cheese cake. I’ll be frank, I’m not a big fan of the dark chocolate soufflé but my bf loved it and I trust his pallets. The cheese cake was amazingly light despite looking so thick. Tastes good too! But thanks to my stupid condition. I can’t eat too much of it lol... but it was a good experience.4. The service was quite attentive and since it’s uncle’s birthday, he got a free dessert which was made of strawberry and cheese. Basically cheese cake 😂 but it’s quite tasty and I actually preferred it over the desserts we ordered. It’s not much but just enough to satisfy me.So overall, the restaurant is great, atmosphere is comfortable and the view is great. But what I don’t like is it’s location since it’s near a residential area so the parking here is awful. Unless ur willing to pay RM 5 an hour, go ahead and park in the hotel. Otherwise, valet which is pricier.

Author: Ryan Liong
Review: Food - no nasty surprises from our orders for a table of 3. Lamb was done medium rare which was cooked well and that's all, and perhaps the fat can be further rendered just a bit more. Cauliflower is on the less interesting side but perhaps …MoreFood - no nasty surprises from our orders for a table of 3. Lamb was done medium rare which was cooked well and that's all, and perhaps the fat can be further rendered just a bit more. Cauliflower is on the less interesting side but perhaps it was meant to be a palate cleanser item. Eggplant had a smokey flavour but was a bit over-smoked for my liking. Escargot in a ball was a clever twist to make it less visually discouraging for one friend but friend no. 2 said the escargot is barely discernible. I'm neutral about it.Definitely not common of French cuisine to have chicken feet among other interesting choices that Asians are familiar with but not so much in the western world. Scoring an A for effort there! We saw our neighbouring table ordered the whole chicken and was struck with a case of food envy. Menu is pretty good for sharing.Price - you should expect the premium is in the ambiance, dining floor level, and renovation. Food alone, probably on the borderline high side for the simple ingredients, in line with the spirit of "entier". Not complaining here...Ambiance - went for dinner, lights were intentionally dimmed for cozy feeling but saw the other table struggling to read the menu under the lighting. Kesian the auntie.There are window seats for big groups, a nice touch.The interior work and finishing was well done. The place feels elegant and music choice was quite appropriate.Service - was largely attentive and professional. Remembered requests like serving coffee until after the meal. Commendable!3.5 stars from me. Google wouldn't let me do that half.
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Sean Hor
Review: I had one of the best experience while I'm here at the Entier restaurant. From the ambience to the service and the food, everything is simply amazing and well deserved a 5 star rating. …MoreI had one of the best experience while I'm here at the Entier restaurant. From the ambience to the service and the food, everything is simply amazing and well deserved a 5 star rating.From the moment I walk in into the restaurant, all the server nearby ,hostess already welcome me and nicely escort me to my table. My seat was by the window side and I must say the view is quite something. Even though, the lighting is quite dim but it brings out the comfort ,relaxing and private feeling when dining in the restaurant.The server here are also very attentive and they quickly responds to all our needs. The server also quite well informed on the ingredients in the menu items and they are able to explains every detail of the menu items like cooking methods, ingredients and even the origin of the ingredients , they obviously did their homework and understand every details. The server that serve me that night I think his name is Yasir, also quite friendly and always be there for my every needs. As this was my first time visit the restaurant but the server was able to provide some good recommendation for me. I also want to give my special thanks to Mr Danil, the manager and Mr Jason, assistant manager as they also very friendly and have some small talks with me on my feedback on the restaurant.As for the food, the food I ordered that night are oxtail soup, lamb chop and mango. Before the food comes, the restaursre also provide a sourdough bread with konbu butter. You can tell that the bread was fresh baked daily and the lobby butter really give a distinct flavour just like truffles. Then, the oxtail soup with the ox tail mantou was a great combination that brings out the best of the oxtail . The mantou bun was very fluffy and soft with the nicely braised meat in the middle, biting it gives a new level of satisfaction. As for the soup, inside the bowl with a spinach ball that filled with oxtail meats as well when cut n mix with the soup , it gives the soup a more rich flavour. Next , for the main is the lamb chop. The Lamb chop was nicely grilled to perfect doneness which I ordered according to the recommendation from the server, which is medium. And the sauce really do bring out the taste of the lamb chop and also is very nice when dip it with the sweet potato chips on the side. Finally, is the dessert mango. The mango sorbet is clearly amazing and filled with sweet and tasty fresh mangoes on the side. Surprisingly, there are also some handmade mocchi in there and it taste very unique.Although all the food is French cuisine but as the headchef is a Japanese, the food was really mixed with a bit of the Japanese culture, making it a really unique French cuisine restaurant.I will definitely recommend Entier for whoever likes French cuisines and like a restaurant with cozy and relaxing environment.
Location: Level 41 at Alila Bangsar No 58, Jalan Ang Seng, Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur

We got a few nods from him before he walked off. I guess we should feel lucky to receive whatever we get. We were charged full price for the honeycomb tripe, which we returned barely eaten and was not even offered an exchange.I don’t know what could have saved flaccid, dispiriting honeycomb beef tripe soaking in a pool of oil, but it definitely wasn’t (literally) a leg of chicken that looks silly and taste worse.The fact that this restaurant is regarded so highly in food blogs and magazines by so-called “food connoisseurs”, and to experience what we did first hand is the systematic dismantling of all my culinary hopes and dreams.Entier is a self-regarding, ungenerous place that should be avoided at all cost.

Review: All I can say is...AMAZING!Words won't help describe my experience there, but I'll try my best. …MoreAll I can say is...AMAZING!Words won't help describe my experience there, but I'll try my best.As recommended, I had Salmon Confit and Dark Chocolate Soufflé. The salmon is really something you should give a try. Its absolutely DELICIOUS! It's moist and owh so delicate, as well as the fact that it literally melts in your mouth! No kidding. Go try it for yourself and you'll know what I'm talking about.As if my mouth wasn't already at its most serene, came the Dark Chocolate Soufflé. That is...FOR SURE, the number 1 reason for my next trip there. It is, to put it lightly, to DIE FOR. Whoever made this must be a magician, because it is truly magical. Warm and fluffy, what else would you need. Owh wait...ICE CREAM. Yes, they serve it with ice cream on a bed of crunchy oats, and I savoured every single bite of that masterpiece. Just mindblowing!And not only is the food great, the service crew was impeccable. They are knowledgeable and swift, polite just as they are friendly. It's as if I never reached the bottom of my glass. Which shows, they are very observant and quick to respond. Have you ever been to a restaurant where everyone feels very uptight? Yeah, you won't be getting that here.I know some didn't get to enjoy their experience as I've had but maybe you shouldn't be too quick to judge. They've only been open for about 4 weeks now. Sure, there might be some things to be tweaked. So why don't you give them another chance. I'm pretty sure you didn't go about your life without a mistake. Maybe you went at a peak time, and the service was a little slow but please be considerate. They only have so many hands to go around.It is really a place to try. I highly recommend going there...even if it's just for their Dark Chocolate Soufflé. And who knows, we might even bump into each other on my next trip there.To the crew, great job! Review: A Traditional Well Balanced Meal with A TwistFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-in …MoreA Traditional Well Balanced Meal with A TwistFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-inService: We ordered via a third party application which was fairly straight forwardPackaging: Arrived in an ordinary looking paper box and plastic bagAustralian M5 Wagyu Ribeye (200g) (RM 148)Taste: Rooted from their years of travel and much experimental comes Asian cuisine with a modern twist. Wagyu is known for its unique texture and melt in your mouth effect. Comparison between Japanese and Australian Wagyu would not be a fair playing field though both are graded similarly. But for a grade 5 wagyu by Australian standards, it had a decent amount of webbing of fat and a creamier feeling in our mouth making us crave for more with each bite. Author: Marc Woo
Review: Agreeable with the rest of the reviews -- overpriced and very ordinary euro (not entirely french) food. …MoreAgreeable with the rest of the reviews -- overpriced and very ordinary euro (not entirely french) food.My experience started off with a polite staff taking my reservation, and in the end asked for 80bux per pax to lock in the booking. So I said I would just walk in, but she mentioned it will be very busy on a Friday night. So I paid. The whole restaurant had 3 tables last Friday ...The food was very average. The cauliflower soup was bland despite having one tiny sea urchin. The Foie gras terrine seemed to me like a normal pork terrine, I could barely taste the liver. The desserts were slightly better with a good balance of flavours and the beetroot refresher was surprisingly the star.The food was tolerable until I found a sharp bone in the sea bream fillet. Totally unexpected (and unacceptable) for a high end french restaurant. I complained to the wait staff and nothing was done. She did not bother to let the chef know and no gesture was made to appease a disgruntled customer. They did message me on WhatsApp after I left to apologise and gave a lame excuse that the wait staff was busy and couldn't find time to let the chef know. Busy with only 3 tables that night? And clearly a sharp bone in a dish does not take priority over serving the other two tables. If this happened in France, the restaurant will be boycotted by the entire nation the very next day.Some reviewers commented on the decor and ambience. I found the hard tiled plain white walls and flooring made for a very noisy night. Again with 3 tables.Negative experience overall. Too pricey for the lackluster food. The honesty quotient is also dubious. Will not return.
Location: 54G & 56G, Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Alan Ooi
Review: Went to Dominic on 5 Dec with my wife it was a lovely Saturday evening. We sat down a decided to order a 5 course meal for the winter and seafood course. There were choices but the waitress actually took the liberty to decide the options …MoreWent to Dominic on 5 Dec with my wife it was a lovely Saturday evening. We sat down a decided to order a 5 course meal for the winter and seafood course. There were choices but the waitress actually took the liberty to decide the options for us as both the menu are almost identical except for the main course.TLDR : food is average, the wait between course is too long, the staff doesn't explain the course when servingSo for the long versionBread - Good, crispy and fluffy at the right place and it's warmAmuse bouche - to be honest can't really taste anything and the bread/base that is use for this is soggy and the crab on it is pretty dull1st coursePate - good, with a slice of very well toasted bread. Nothing could go wrong. Pate was fatty and it wasn't too pungent (bizzare experience here. The wait staff came up to me with 3 bowls of salt and didn't really explained to me what were they and asked me what do I want for the pate?. I was blanked and I have to asked the staff to explain what were they)Tuna noodles? - good, the tuna flavour was overwhelmed by the vinaigrette taste. Although the pickled radish was a welcoming addition to the dish2nd courseHamachi I think? - average and frankly pretty boring. It's just fish and not even fantasticCream of cauliflower?- average, it's different because of the jelly in the middle of the soup. But frankly that jelly doesn't have any flavour and it doesn't add anything to the texture either3rd courseSome fish - average, again it's a fish dish that is very average nothing to shout aboutScallops - bad, unfortunately for this course I was really having higher hopes for as fresh scallops usually have the sweetness and a very pleasant texture to it. This scallops was not it. Can't taste any of the scallops flavour. This one really fall flat4th courseWagyu beef - bad, I'm just going straight to the point here. The beef is chewy and doesn't carry any flavour. The truffle is tasteless. This is my far the worst course in the menuAnother scallops - bad, again same review as above there's nothing special and doesn't taste fresh5th coursePistachio ice cream dessert - good, this one is the best course for the night.Cheese platter - average, it's cheese the selection is alright, there are 5 or 6 cheeses for you to choose 3 and the condiments that comes with it are also alrightOverall, I would give this place another try but not anytime soon. They need to improve on the interval between courses, 30 mins between courses is unacceptable and the wait staff needs to be able to explain the courses properly.I do want to support local restaurant but there are so much to do
Location: 54G & 56G, Jalan Doraisamy, Chow Kit, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Kaberi Dutta
Review: Really incredible food and impeccable service - would definitely return. I had the duck confit for my main …MoreReally incredible food and impeccable service - would definitely return. That being said, the prices are on the higher side so this restaurant may be more suited for special occasions (for me at least!). I had the duck confit for my main and the duck was incredibly tender and perfectly cooked. My only qualm is I wish that they accompanied it with a bit more (maybe potatoes/ some sort of purée?) but other than that, it was incredible. The escargot meat itself wasn’t the best I’ve had in KL but the sauce it comes in is amazing - make sure you save some bread to have with it! Author: j p
Review: After a 40-minute attempt, including 28 phone dialing’s to make a reservation…I GAVE UP…and I am SO GLAD that I did…in my attempt to eat at Restaurant “X” elsewhere in KL. …MoreAfter a 40-minute attempt, including 28 phone dialing’s to make a reservation…I GAVE UP…and I am SO GLAD that I did…in my attempt to eat at Restaurant “X” elsewhere in KL.Super frustrated, I searched TripAdvisor for an alternate FRENCH RESTAURANT.  AS A former 3.5-year resident of Paris, I was craving a few things…1) great TRADITIONAL French food, 2) a place to grab that nice meal on a casual Saturday and 3) to treat two friends after a year of Covid-mania!Our reservation for three was made a week ahead of time.  We entered at 12:30, first one’s there and were given a table we did not like.  “May we change tables please?”   “Yes…how about the window?”…YES nicer!  HAMMER HAMMER HAMMER!  The hammering next door was on the other side of the wall (reno of the next-door shop)…and we asked them to have them stop…and they did! RELEIVED!The space has a large main dining space and a somewhat separate bar are. The wood floors, bright white walls showcasing colorful art, and rich red velour dividing curtains make for a bright, and comfortable space.Seeing that my friend owns a fine wine import business in KL, he surprised me with two very nice French reds, 2013 and 2014 Bordeaux!  The corkage fee is RM80 per bottle and we had some nice wine so worth it.  We two arrived first while our third trailed us a bit, so we had some Pellegrino and opened a bottle of wine to let it breath.The Lunch menu has TWO fixed-prix menus, PLUS ala carte, plus a large wine and drinks list.  The fixed RM140 menu is truly an offering of a starter, main course and a desert.  The second RM170 fixed menu offers a starter, a main with a bit extra RM for three of the mains (a bit sneaky we thought). A lovely bread and Pesto Olive Oil dip were brought…perhaps a bit too late.We all three ordered a la carte…as we wanted to try some other things to share like the ratatouille (we ordered to share among three, perfect!).Our selections:We shared two orders of the Ratatouille and a large Pellegrino.1)	Lobster Bisque > the Larger Wagyu steak w potatoes and gravy > Crepes Suzette > Double Espresso2)	French Onion Soup Souffle > Lobster Ravioli > Crepes Suzette > An Espresso3)	French Onion Soup Souffle > the Larger Wagyu steak > Crepes Suzette > A Double SambucaALL the dishes were delicious…the service staff, neatly dressed in black, were attentive, friendly, and responsive.  My meal arrived a bit on the cold side and I sent it back for a fast zap, something to address.We were at our table from 12:30 to 3:00 and never felt rushed…until we were admittedly a bit surprised to learn that the kitchen closing at 3:00pm meant we also had to evacuate the premises…while still having sambuca or wine or espresso still to consume.  The time frames painted on the front door perhaps needs editing.  We were welcome to finish our drinks on the front terrace, which we did, while we ordered a grab home.I would definitely consider this ONE OF THE VERY BEST MEALS that I have enjoyed in 6+ years in KL.I will definitely return.  The menu’s appeal means that it is likely meal options, water, wine and coffees may make a small dent in the wallet, so choose wisely and savor the meal.

Review: I’m not big on Middle Eastern food but you don’t need to be an aficionado to appreciate good food. …MoreI’m not big on Middle Eastern food but you don’t need to be an aficionado to appreciate good food.Went to BEDOUIN in the neighbourhood of Taman Tun Dr. Ismail (Kuala Lumpur) for dinner with a few friends. A good start to the meal.- Second salad was simply fresh sliced tomato and pickled gherkins with sprigs of mint on the side.2 Mains:- A lava stone cooked spiced beef and onion dry stew.  My favourite dish for the night. A dish wiped clean by the end of the meal.- A lamb shank mandi (Middle Eastern styled biryani).  Rice was very well prepared.  Mutton had good natural flavour and the right tenderness.  I would have liked a wee bit more salt on the lamb but that’s just me.  My dining companions found it just perfect (as can be seen from the cleaned out bone). 🤣A “support” dish of baked unleavened bread sprinkled with sesame seed toppings and some hummus dip.  This bread is in my opinion another absolute highlight of the meal.  Yummy.Ended the meal with some caramel custard.  I felt texture was a little rough but still soft and appetising.  The taste of the accompanying sauce was good.  Not just a straight forward caramel sweetness, it had some hints of underlying complexity.  I thought I tasted hints of orange.Overall - Very satisfying meal.  I’ll certainly be back.  👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻I’ve read some reviews that mention slow food/service.  I experienced impeccable and knowledgeable service.  So absolutely no complaints.  Some of the food served is what I will call “slow cooked food”, food that is at is best when prepared on order and served fresh. It will take some time so perhaps allocate a good amount of time to fully enjoy the Bedouin experience.@whiskydev

My friend had a mint tea, and the other a fresh pineapple juice.The bread is to die for. Order a size bigger than you think, because it is simply yum. My three faves were the bread, beans and aubergine. If I went by myself, I’d order that and be happy.For the rest, I thoroughly enjoyed it all except for the boiled lamb. It was tender, falling off the bone, but it’s just not as nice as a roast. My friends disagreed, they loved the lamb. We polished off the lot, and it cost us about RM40 per person.Pleasant, friendly service and a very pretty restaurant. Definitely a place to take people if you want to entertain.Park in the big building next door or across the street in TTDI market and walk 100 meters because street parking here is absolute hell.

Author: Roy Yap
Review: The idea of it sounds really great. Refurbish an old airplane and turn it into a fine dining restaurant. For many including myself, this is as close as you are going to get to dining on a first class flight. …MoreThe idea of it sounds really great. Refurbish an old airplane and turn it into a fine dining restaurant. For many including myself, this is as close as you are going to get to dining on a first class flight.To complete the experience, you need to check in at the departure lounge though there isn't much to do while waiting for your "flight". You can order drinks while you wait but unless you paid for the upgraded experience, the drinks are chargeable.There are about 12 tables in the plane itself, each sits 2 diners. The seats do resemble somewhat like first class seats on an airplane but to be honest they are not really the most comfortable when you need to lean forward to eat from a table and not from an attached tray.Food is quite good and there is unlimited refill of juice and water. Unfortunately, unlike on a real plane, there is no free flow of alcoholic drinks. Bummer.During the event there are multiple times when you will be asked to take photos. At check in, while dining and also during the cockpit visit. While they are nice enough to offer to take photos using your camera/phone, photos taken by the restaurant's photographer are sold at quite exorbitant prices. While the rest of the experience seemed very high class, the sale of photos reeked of AirAsia's nickel and diming practice and soured the whole experience for me. A better idea would be to email the photos to the guests as a souvenir or memorabilia.

Review: Four Seasons features a collection of romantic menus throughout Curate, Pool Bar & Grill, The Lounge, and Decadent this Valentine’s Day. These restaurants offer the best experiences for couples looking for a romantic dining experience to …MoreFour Seasons features a collection of romantic menus throughout Curate, Pool Bar & Grill, The Lounge, and Decadent this Valentine’s Day. These restaurants offer the best experiences for couples looking for a romantic dining experience to celebrate birthdays, anniversaries, and any other special occasions.At Four Seasons Kuala Lumpur, romantic experiences and custom menus that are specially tailored to your preferences are available all day, not just on Valentine’s Day.Their philosophy: “Treat others the way you would want to be treated” is promising and so is their reputation. Slightly informal setting, you get to choose from a semi circle lounge chairs to low sofa and tables and a unique 7 seater table cut from a huge piece of marble.Service was excellent. Prompt, professional, helpful and friendly. The Nasi Lemak Surf and Turf was unique. Comes with beef rib rendang and half lobster cooked in sambal. The dish  wasn't hot but well marinated and seasoned with spices. A good complex taste from the succulent beef rib rendang and tender meat from half a lobster cooked in sambal. The sambal coated the lobster meat well.The wagyu beef burger was also amazing. Cooked medium rare or to your liking, the marbelling or fat intertwined in the beef to make the burger moist enough but a layer of sauteed onions and mushrooms helped out with the taste. Portion was sizeable for one or if you're a small eater, share it with another.To get the most of the burger, you need to cut a slice of the burger with the bun and onions and mushroom, eat it while slicing a small piece of pickle and combining it with the burger and the taste comes together. The fatty Wagyu beef, the sauteed onions, the mushrooms and the pickle perfectly compliments each other.For dessert, if you love strawberry cheesecake, then this is the one for you. The best strawberry cheesecake I've tasted so far. The base is crunchy and tasty, the cheese wasn't too sweet and the imported fresh strawberries was juicy and sweet. Still salivating while I'm typing this.Truly an amazing experience at The Lounge with the live piano (apologies because I thought it was from a CD) as it was very good. Overall experience, loved it. Will definitely come back again.

Author: Piger Woods
Review: I am not usually one for negative reviews because I know the struggles of running a small business but in this case I feel it is necessary. Given all the positive reviews, I was really looking forward to having a proper Sunday breakfast …MoreI am not usually one for negative reviews because I know the struggles of running a small business but in this case I feel it is necessary. Given all the positive reviews, I was really looking forward to having a proper Sunday breakfast here today. I even brought my backpack in anticipation of loading up my freezer at home. All in all, it was pretty disappointing. There were only 3 tables occupied when we got there, yet still it was around 20 minutes before our order was taken. We both ordered the Scottish breakfast because of the tattie scones and wanted additional black pudding and toast on the side. We were told there was no black pudding or even mushrooms. We were given a choice of 2 sausage types, I chose Cajun because I like a bit of spice. When the plates arrived, the tattie scone turned out to be just a triangle of fried, unseasoned, mashed potato which was mushy and very oily. No relation to a tattie scone at all. I like my eggs runny but the whites were still uncooked, very unappetising. The Cajun sausage had absolutely no flavour, not even salt, never mind spice and there was no real texture to make you feel that you were eating a quality product...just nothing. In fact the whole plate was really bland, no seasoning or flavour at all. Worse still, the sausage was raw in the middle and I left it. Surprising for a place called SausageKL. My toast didn't come so I had to ask for it and when it did arrive, it was barely warm and looked like it had been wafted over a 40 watt bulb for 5 seconds to toast it. The bacon consisted of two very small, overcooked rashers which again, had no real flavour. I can understand it if one of the items on a plate is not up to scratch but not a single element of the breakfast plate was done properly. A full cooked breakfast, when done correctly is a wonderful thing, in fact I make a pretty good one myself but when you take the time to go somewhere that specialises in this, you expect it to be good and it really, really wasn't. Our friends at the other table felt the same way. On the upside, the mug of tea was decent. They could have been having an off day today but I don't think so and I very much doubt I will go again to find out. Based on my experience today, I couldn't, in good conscience recommend SausageKL to anyone I know. I am certainly confused as to where all the positive reviews are coming from. Not good at all...My search for a decent cooked breakfast in KL continues...

Author: Alfredo L.
Review: Truly 5 stars. I’ve eaten at many, many Michelin starred restaurants and honestly Lai Po Heen is worthy of one. Heck, this would be considered fantastic even by mainland Chinese standards. …MoreTruly 5 stars. I’ve eaten at many, many Michelin starred restaurants and honestly Lai Po Heen is worthy of one. Heck, this would be considered fantastic even by mainland Chinese standards.The food: I had a tasting menu featuring items like lobster in coconut sauce, braised duck leg, abalone soup, and a durian dessert platter.Each course was prepared immaculately. Crab was clearly fresh and seasoned well. The lobster was succulent and juicy while being well seasoned. The shell cracked perfectly so the meat would fall right out. The duck leg you could cut with a spoon and seasoned perfectly. The abalone soup was perfectly delicate with just the right amount of salinity. The durian desserts showcased the pungent flavor of durian without letting it overpower you.Service was also spectacular. My tea cup was never empty, finished courses were promptly ferried away, and fresh silverware was provided for the dishes that most required it. I felt I was being well attended to without being overwhelmed.Yes, it’s expensive. No, it’s not meant to be perfectly authentic— local flavors are definitely showcased here and fused with traditional Chinese classics. But it’s absolutely worth it. Whoever manages Lai Po Heen deserves a pat on the back— this is a world class dining experience.My only (minor) complaint would be that I wish the dress code was a bit more enforced. Not to the point of jacket and tie but I did see people there with Hawaiian shirts, flip flops, and cargo shorts. Kinda kills the vibe a bit.
Location: Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

I ordered 2 items the saba curry risotto set & their premium gyoza starter. The starter apparently was sold out so I didn't receive it. The saba is a hit & miss for me. Some aspects of the fish I liked & there are aspects which I didn't. Portion size is ok ok. If u're a large eater this ain't gonna fill u up. The saba didn't look appetizing but it has a nice crispy skin and it was fresh so no real complaints here. My only gripe with the dish was the curry risotto. It was sadly under seasoned and I didn't get much of a curry flavour coming through. The accompanying tea was refreshing- nice. So to be fair I'm gonna give a average rating till I can actually get there and dine in for a proper rating. Will update later
