Author: N Y
Review: Read about the good reviews and decided to try this restaurant out after eating pho at pho king. It did not disappoint. With our limited stomach, We only ordered 2 dishes, petai with prawns and fried chicken. The food was home cooked nonya …MoreRead about the good reviews and decided to try this restaurant out after eating pho at pho king. It did not disappoint. With our limited stomach, We only ordered 2 dishes, petai with prawns and fried chicken. The food was home cooked nonya style that brought back fond memories of my grandma’s food. Requested for sambal to go with the fried chicken and it was also good. Wish they could make the sambal spicier with some lime juice. For 15rm, we had enough petai with prawns to serve 2. Fried chicken was also 15 rm. The chicken was well marinated and fried nicely such that it was crispy on the outside but still juicy on the inside! It went perfectly with the chilli petai udang. If I live nearby, I may come like once a week cause it tasted like home. Ala carte items were not available on public holiday and weekends. We were left with less choices but it was more than enough for 2 of us to go home with fond memories.
Location: 129, Jalan SS 2/6, SS 2, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Kakistocracy
Review: A very quaint but a Penangites foodie delight is all I can say about this joint. Looks like it needs more publicity, advertising and a new PR person and lesson revision. In this part of town Penangites are few especially groups. When I …MoreA very quaint but a Penangites foodie delight is all I can say about this joint. Looks like it needs more publicity, advertising and a new PR person and lesson revision. In this part of town Penangites are few especially groups. When I dropped by with my family in tow or rather they towed me including my 7 month old grandaughter totalling 7 hungry ghost. The owners daughter cum restaurant manager didnt as much as acknowledge us a smile , while the "towkay"/owner was busy blabbering away with 2 probably freeloading buddies. I could have sworn that I being a born n bred Penangite could have find a connection between my wifes family n me and this "towkay" probably school chums. He and his daughter were busy blabbering away, never welcoming customers, more so from their very own "Dalcha Penang" country. That is about the service - from the owners not waiters.Now the choice of Penang style Malay/ Mamak/Chinese fusion food makes my eyes swell up in tears as only  a true Pgite can understand. Some of the dishes I have not eaten since my teenage years. My family knows I have a small appetite but this time around , I ordered the "nyonya laksa" , ( there is also a choice of assam laksa),  cendol kacang ( ori minus the ice cream), "pasembor" and "rojak" ( for non Pgite guess what is which?)   my family ordered nasi " daging khorma", "ayam ros", "ayam masak kicap" and one family member who had never grew up in Penang ordering the universal fav "ayam goreng".  My nyonya laksa, I "demanded" Penang all time favorite foul rotten fish smelling " side dish" that is a must on Penang island - the "otak udang", ("petis",shrimp paste,) it is a must have for in any Penang assam laksa but not on mainland. FYI mainland "assam laksa" version is what was dubbed as "laksa Melayu". The ingredients are basically the same except that the Penang version includes shrimp paste as its ingredient , the Malay version excludes it and add a half boiled eggs as its topping. My taste buds are for my original assam laksa Air Itam style.( I know the exact ingredient) and not laksa melayu.If you can ignore the owners arrogance and just focus on the dishes this place offers the most extensive Malay/Mamak/Chinese fusion dish spread. I was expecting the standard answer "we dont serve this and that anymore" but the kitchen just churn out the dishes, I suspect some from deep freeze but serve they did. Kudos to whoever is the Chef and minus kudos to the owner for their customer service. If I were you I would hurry up before the owners luck runs out.
Restaurant: Dalca Penang Restaurant by Masakan Warisan
Location: 35, Jalan 8/152, Taman Perindustrian Oug, Kuala Lumpur, Selangor

Review: Mediterranean dishes at its best!As I passed by this restaurant everytime after I finished having my coffee at …MoreMediterranean dishes at its best!As I passed by this restaurant everytime after I finished having my coffee at Cream nearby, I recalled on a Mediterranean restaurant that I used to go in Mont Kiara a long time ago. A quick check confirmed that they have moved to Dataran Prima in PJ.Wondering how they have changed after all these years, I made a reservation for dinner one Saturday evening. While it was almost impossible to find a parking here on normal working days, it's almost deserted come evening and weekends.Striking a casual yet cosy atmosphere, the waiters made our visit welcome by their higher-than-average service. Armed with a bottle of Spanish Tempranillo, the evening has just got better.◾sous vide white pork ribs - it felt like Chinese style braised pork ribs but delicious nonetheless.◾smoked chicken croquettes - served lollipop style. I just picked up the skewer and took one whole ball into the mouth.◾bacon & melted mozzarella sandwich with semi-dried tomatoes - visually striking and inviting, most probably due to the bacon on a bed of melted cheese on top of the crusty, crunchy yet light sourdough bread. Fold and eat away. Served with a bowl of fries.◾Basic pasta - penne in pesto sauce without any topping at RM24. The daughter declared that the pesto sauce was one of the best she'd ever tried.◾Margarita pizza - RM30.. initially thinking how on earth were we going to finish the pizza given that we'd ordered so many items, we somehow managed to finish the delicious and competently prepared pizza. The crust was simply lovely in texture.◾Seafood risotto with semi-dried tomato sauce - at RM42, this was the most expensive risotto in the menu◾Pan seared foie gras - by far the most expensive dish of the evening at RM82 for 50g liver. A rather big piece of foie gras perfectly cooked served on a bed of salad. Honestly it was not enough for both of us.By the end of the dinner, all of us agreed that this place deserved to be in my permanent to-go list.

Author: Ge Chu hua
Review: For years, Thai Thai Restaurant in Sunway Pyramid has been serving diners in with their finest Thai cuisines and hospitality service. In order to provide a better dining environment, Thai Thai goes through a series of renovation this year, …MoreFor years, Thai Thai Restaurant in Sunway Pyramid has been serving diners in with their finest Thai cuisines and hospitality service. In order to provide a better dining environment, Thai Thai goes through a series of renovation this year, and now they are back again with their brand new dining environment, but same delicious and authentic Thai delicacies.The newly renovated Thai Thai emphasizes on simple, modern yet elegant interior, but retaining the Thai concept at the same time. The next time when you dine in Thai Thai, do keep an eye on the colourful “symbols” that are mingle on the black coloured walls, they are Thai words.We went for a Thai feast in Thai Thai when it is opened back after the renovation, and feel glad that their food is still good as before.There are a few signature drinks (House Speciallity) in Thai Thai which you should not miss, which are Thai Iced Tea, Thai Iced Coffee, Thai Thai Fruit Punch, Iced Blended Fresh Coconut, Iced Blended Lychee Mint and Mango Mama Smoothies.Thai Iced Tea – Back (RM10.00)Thai Iced Tea emphasizes more on the tea flavor, where the milk taste is tone down with the distinct tea flavor. Good for those who like their milk tea to be in stronger tea flavor.We started off the meal with Thod Man Pla, or Thai Fish Cake which serves as a great snack before the mains. The fish cakes have a firm and bouncy texture, and you can dip it into sweet chilli sauce served alongside with the fish cake for extra flavors.

Author: Stephen Abraham
Review: An authentic Thai restaurant serving premium Thai food. Price is quite high, the flavors are above average, but not fantastic. When we arrived, looking through the menu, all the food items were called in their original Thai names. At least …MoreAn authentic Thai restaurant serving premium Thai food. Price is quite high, the flavors are above average, but not fantastic. When we arrived, looking through the menu, all the food items were called in their original Thai names. At least there were explanations and photos. Naming the food in their original names set quite a high expectation for us, since we frequent Bangkok and have eaten fantastic food there at much lower cost. To start off, we ordered the fried fish cakes with the sweet Thai chilly sauce and the papaya salad (Som Tam Thai). The fish cakes were alright. The papaya salad seems to be missing something that we could not place. Maybe we were used to so much more spice in Thailand. Then we had the pineapple fried rice, green chicken curry, Tom Yam Gung and some fried vegetables. Taste was good. Main dish was the steamed Siakap. That was alright. For dessert we had the mango with sticky rice which was nice, and the water chestnut in coconut milk which was good too. Overall, the restaurant setting was inviting, and relaxing. Staff were quite helpful and tried their best to give their best service. I can't say if I would come back very often. Still give it a try if you want authentic Thai food and don't mind stretching your wallet a little.
Location: Jalan PJS 11/15, Bandar Sunway, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Review: Haven't had such a unique gastronomical experience like this before, and Kayra delivers it well. No wonder why it was listed as one of the top 20 restaurants on Tatler Dining list in 2021. No wonder why it was listed as one of the top 20 restaurants on Tatler Dining list in 2021. Well-deserved!It's worth a try for those looking for authentic Kerala cuisines and would like to try something other than banana leaf rice (Indian food isn't just about banana leaf rice by the way 😆). Their sea bass is tender and fresh, while their dosa taco is a unique take on the traditional tacos! As Chinese, I've always had our claypot chicken rice growing up and never tasted the Indian version of it, and it didn't disappoint. It's extremely different from Chinese claypot rice as this one is coated with curry and various types of veggies.Their beverage menu is quite interesting too, but I was less adventurous and only went with Mango Lassi, which is rich and creamy, and it met my expectations.Overall Kayra was an eye-opener to me. Will absolutely bring any food adventurer here for a celebration. Keep it up, Kayra!

Basically we ordered the usually dim sum such as the siew mai, prawn dumplings, many more. The only difference here they offer is the Dao Xiao Mian, which means knife-shaven noodles, is a specialty of Shanxi Province. The most authentic technique for making dao xiao mian is to hold a large block of dough downwards with one hand at about a 30-degree angle. The other hand, clutching a sharp knife (that’s specifically made for this purpose) shaves the noodles directly into a large pot of boiling water. It takes years of practice to cut the noodles quickly – it is believed that a top chef can shave 200 noodle strands a minute.Overall the food was delicious and tasty. There’s only 2 issues here. Service was bad as they are short of captains on the floor. Trying to get someone to take care of our order was so hard. They are very well short handed. The other issue is the price which is bit high comparing to others. Author: Anastasia Soh
Review: Chinese Comfort Food within The Comforts & Safety of HomeFirst off, this is a review on their delivery service and not dine-in. …MoreChinese Comfort Food within The Comforts & Safety of HomeFirst off, this is a review on their delivery service and not dine-in.Being the exclusive few Taiwanese restaurants to be awarded a Michelin Star, Ding Tai Fung requires no introduction. We have dined in their branches across South East Asia & have always departed with a satisfied & full tummy. But how do they fare in a take away?Service: We placed the order via a third party app hence was pretty straight forward.Packaging: Nothing much to rave about with ordinary take away boxes✅ Prawn with Salted Egg (RM 45.47)Taste: Despite having sat in a delivery box and exposed to the evils of a typical delivery such as moisture and a very reckless rider, the dish still arrived piping hot & intact. The prawns were fresh giving us a delightful crunch as we sank our teeth into it with the flavourful salted egg batter crispy on the outside & drizzled with chilli.Price: Reasonable 🙆🏻‍♀️✅ Pork Chop Fried Rice (RM 26.29)Taste: Each grain of rice had a very smooth texture, evenly coated with egg & oil from the pork & sprinkled with chives.  Rested on the top is a succulent pork chop which was slightly charred on the edges yet juicy within & sprinkled with pepper. The pork chop was seasoned beautifully, resulting in a well balanced dish which wasn’t too salty.Price: Reasonable 🙆🏻‍♀️✅ Sweet & Sour Chicken (RM 29.47)Taste: They separated the sauce from the stir fried meat & peppers hence the meat, peppers & onions were still crunchy upon arrival & gave us the pleasure of pouring the sauce over the dish. The sauce was a little sweet especially with the onions already providing a tinge of sweetness to the dish with a splash of lemon balancing the whole dish beautifully.Price: Reasonable 🙆🏻‍♀️Recommended? Ding Tai Fung has been a crowd favourite & comfort food to some for years. Despite facing the challenges of a delivery service, they have not disappointed🙆🏻‍♀️Our full review is on Instagram ( @monk3yseendo )
Restaurant: Din Tai Fung 鼎泰豐 at Pavilion KL
Location: Lot 6 .01.05, Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, 168, Bukit Bintang St, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Swiss
Review: This place has been around way back since my secondary school days. Perhaps, this place evokes nostalgic feeling, which kept me returning to the shop whenever I am around the area looking for a light breakfast or banana leaf lunch

Author: Louis Lee
Review: Best Roti Chenai/prata by Raju. Very famous in KL.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Jaisharan Gill

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Amy Tan

Author: indigo blue

Author: SA 30

Author: Mohd. Ramesh
Review: Food is quite tasty, but pricey
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Adam Marchione
Review: I went on a hike at Gasing Hill with my good old friend, Britney Spears. Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Rudy Loh

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: amalen sathananthar
Review: Good food. very pleasant service.  had banana leaf rice. vegetables were yummy and plentiful. mutton chap was da bomb.fried squid couldve been better tasting in terms of the batter they used, cooked very well though.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Lim Tzu Hsiong
Review: Nice food, especially nice fried chicken and sotong. Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Wong Choon Jiat
Review: Went to the restaurant in the morning. It was crowded with people even on a the eve of CNY. Ordered the a normal thosai and one masala thosai. The taste was good as we can see each piece was freshly prepared pair together with dal and curry.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Izrin Muaz Md Adnan
Review: The rava thosai and roti kosong are brilliant. The tea was less successful, too milky and not strong as I would prefer my tea to be.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Halim Mohd Nor
Review: The roti canai was goodThe sotong was good
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Rattan Roy
Review: Food was alright, served us cold rice, chicken and fish cold curries (watered down) for our banana leaf. It was 4pm so it's ok, no fuss for us. What we could not stand is the flies. Author: Julian Lee
Review: Very bad service. The boss is a nice lady but I feel she has no control over her workers. Author: Taamaraiselvi Chinathamby
Review: Ate here again after 10 years. Still soo good

Author: Ryan Tay Yi Wen

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: SY Chan
Review: Had the banana leaf rice on a sunday last month. The fried fish was perfect, juicy inside and crispy on the outside - 5 stars. Took 2 stars off for the lazily made curry gravy. All 3 types of gravy offered were watered down and flavourless - curry powder and boiled water  concoctions.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Cheng Hwee Chee
Review: Good roti canai place. Also tried the tosai. Popular spot but disappointed that there is no more outside seating.  Like the unlimited dal and coconut sauce. You help yourself to the sauces.  Since the place is crowded you get a sense they are trying to rush you out when you have finished eating.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Saiful Jazri Zahari
Review: I haven't been to Raju's for quite a while and was shocked to see the outdoor seating area is gone. No longer are we able to sit under the cool shade of large trees and enjoy our roti canai, roti telur, fried cuttlefish, chicken and …MoreI haven't been to Raju's for quite a while and was shocked to see the outdoor seating area is gone. No longer are we able to sit under the cool shade of large trees and enjoy our roti canai, roti telur, fried cuttlefish, chicken and mackeral with the cool hillside breeze.  The municipal built a large monsoon drain taking away the space for all fresco dining.Nevertheless even with 70% less dining area, the food is still remarkable. The curry is elegant and not strong and overpowering like some other restaurants. The fried cuttlefish is mild in taste and the deep fried chicken still shines through its freshness.Customer turnover is fast so even though the restaurant looks full, there will be a space in a short while. Service has improved as well due to the smaller seating area and less patrons to serve at one time.Still a good place satisfy your Indian banana leaf food cravings.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Tan TM
Review: Good roti canal. We had the grilled sotong (very good) and fried chicken (mediocre) too. Usually very busy in the morning so prepared to wait for a table.

Author: Potriyan

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: thomas lee

Author: Ian Prakash

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: fazly fariq

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Baargavan Narayanan

Author: Wong Weng Keng
Review: Nice food but price also good
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Paul L

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Ruby Tan

Author: John Lee

Author: olivier Magail

Author: Marcus Foo

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Nick Prior

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Ramaiah Paidiah

Author: Afiq Wan

Author: Azhar Paat

The tasty Teh Tarik blend with your meal.

Author: Pubalan Kumaravelu
Review: Been to Raju's many time and never experienced any disappoinment. The food is always good especially the roti canai. The roti canai is so good that you can eat as lunch meals. The waiters are good and I am sure you will not regret coming here
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Aotearoa Downuder (Aeteorea Downuder)

Author: Mufaddal Zanzibarwala
Review: It's our usual breakfast place after hiking at Gasing Hill on Sundays..... If you're lucky they'll garing the roti canai for you.... It is worth every calorie..... Author: Elaine Loo

Author: Joe Shahabuddin

Author: Soffian Abd. Manaf

Author: YP

Author: F Liu

Author: Bee Lin Ong

Author: Surjit Rai

Author: CH Ngoh

Author: shanthi Nadarajah
Review: Most of the indian eateries in pj are a let down. This one ranks as one of the low one. Menu is the same as any other.  They do not want to serve food that takes more time. Author: Jan Fong

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Wilson Tan Kah Meng
Review: Try the mutton chops. They are to die for. Pricing is very reasonable given that it is Indian Banana Leaf rice. Worth the calories and the price you pay for a wonderful Indian cuisine treat.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: 360 Navigate
Review: A popular destination for PJ folk looking for a late breakfast on the weekend or for some that have just finished a hike nearby. While seating capacity is now less after public facility piping works closed off its former outdoor space, it …MoreA popular destination for PJ folk looking for a late breakfast on the weekend or for some that have just finished a hike nearby. While seating capacity is now less after public facility piping works closed off its former outdoor space, it remains a favourite spot for many.Parking is a problem, so many park around the neighbourhood. The number of spaces around its shoplot number less than 20. Small two lane roads also make things more tedious.The whole-day but mainly breakfast staple of Roti Canai is arguably the best compared to other places. It's always fresh and notably a lot more 'garing' than 90% of the mamak shops you'll go to in Malaysia.There's also banana leaf rice if you fancy, and other favourites here include the deep fried squid with onions and deep fried fish. the price is steeper over at Raju's in comparison to other Mamak shops, but its not really a Mamak shop in all honesty. And well, they have a small sign at their cashier counter that says:"We have no quarrel with competitors who charge less. After all they know what their food is worth."A bold claim, visit yourself and be the judge.

Author: Ben G
Review: This restaurant has been here for ages, but their roti is still as good. Although there's no more dining under the tree, it still draws the breakfast crowd every weekend.
Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Ainur Zurfiqa

Location: 27, Jalan Chantek 5/13, Bukit Gasing, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Dawn C.

Author: Muhammad Asyraf

After having one meal here, I have so many questions about this place.1) This cafe only opens on Friday to Sunday. I asked the staff, why open only from Friday to Sunday? They said they lack staff to run this cafe on weekdays like...PJ is not a cheap place to rent right?2) They don't do takeaways. I understand that takeaways contribute to a lot of non-biodegradable waste but if you don't do takeaways can you at least be explicit with it somewhere in the cafe?3) The Sweet Potato Rosti and Chicken Karange (RM24) - What seasoning did you use that my mouth tastes like Original Pringles after eating this? Its so unbelievably delicious.4) Are you guys a Hygge cafe? My meal took about 20 minutes to arrive. I guess you guys want us to chill and take our time to relax while you guys prepare your beautifully artistic meal? I'm not even being sarcastic here.5) No cashless payments - Like, seriously? When everyone is going cashless these days, you expect your clientele, who is from the upper class to go to an ATM machine, get like RM200++ and hand you cash, old fashion style?I wouldn't mind coming back here again, but I've to prepare myself with CASH and TIME to come here again

Author: Karen D'Cruz
Review: I am born in Malaysia so Sri Lankan cuisine is very new to my taste, and there are very few specialized cafes offering Sri Lankan cuisine. The Lankan Cafe is in the heart of Petaling Garden, situated on the 1st floor of a corner shoplot. …MoreI am born in Malaysia so Sri Lankan cuisine is very new to my taste, and there are very few specialized cafes offering Sri Lankan cuisine. The Lankan Cafe is in the heart of Petaling Garden, situated on the 1st floor of a corner shoplot. The stairs are not steep, and it is a family condusive place.I went there for a Sunday breakfast and was thoroughly amazed at the simplicity of the breakfast menu yet the exquisite and intricate blend of spices for the curries. Sri Lankan curries are spicy and peppery rather than intense chilli, hence it is a treat to the tastebuds for spice-seekers.We tried the Pol Roti, which is a Sri Lankan recipe. It looks like thick paratha on the outside, with a savoury bite of coconut and onions on the inside. I had the Idiappam( puttumayam/stringhoppers) with fish curry. The curry is thick with a peppery taste and a slight sour undertone of lovely tamarind. The thick yellow gravy with coconut milk and a slight peppery taste called Sodhi was also served. Review: Where do you go to satisfy oyster craving? If you happen to be in shopping malls, high chance that you'd say Shucked Oyster Bar. I vaguely remember that it was my ex that introduced me to this. It has aphrodisiac properties.. she said. That was how I got hooked to squeeze lemon and a dallop of tabasco on top of the oysters before devouring it. I used to think that the bigger the better (ehem!) until I learned that it's important how the quality of oysters are affected by various factors such as seawater, etc.Which brings back to Southern Rock Seafood. You'll see no less than 5 types of oysters on the counter, each with different characteristics and prices. Apart from oysters they also serve other types of seafood.◾We started off with half dozen of Irish Premium oysters - meaty & sweet with mellow marine taste. I would have ordered second tray if my tummy permits.◾Clams and mussels in white wine sauce◾Roasted mixed seafood - what to complain if everything is done just right?◾Seafood chowder - spicy tomato based seafood bliss...I'd brought along one of my finest white burgundy just to pair with the delectable seafood and it certainly lifted the mood up. Do take note that corkage charges apply and they also sell a lot of white wines, bubbly and red wine in house.

I would however suggest ordering the fresh one instead of the frozen because the texture was what was lacking from our order.

Review: Review of  their  Fishmonger retail shop attached to the cafe at Bangsar:BEWARE!After a splendid and enjoyable oyster and wine splurge previously at one of this …MoreReview of  their  Fishmonger retail shop attached to the cafe at Bangsar:BEWARE!After a splendid and enjoyable oyster and wine splurge previously at one of this same companies Shucked Oyster bar outlets,we decided to visit their retail shop at Bangsar to take some oysters home to our hotel to have with wine later.All was good,a clean shop,well lit,chatty counter boy,so we ordered 2 dz shucked oysters to go.The english owner popped in from their cafe attached next door,and introduced him self,and the counter boy produced a nice fat just shucked juicy oyster shucked for me to try to show the quality of the product/species I had just orderedWhile chatting with the owner, the oysters were being shucked in the background,and were eventually presented all nicely packed,with ice bag inside and in a sealed insulated foam bin for me to take home where I placed them in the frig.Then to my horror just the next day,with our wine at the ready,on opening the insulated container to find 2 dozen totally inedible dead and severely dehydrated shrunk oysters barely clinging to the half shell,obviously well over the hill and many weeks past life.So the moral of this story,is WATCH what is packaged up here,no matter the distractions.Sorry to have to complain ,but it was inexcusable!

Author: Ruben Kumar M
Review: This authentic Thai establishment is located at ground floor of The School, Jaya One. The restaurant is huge with stall-like concepts of all the dishes offered here. There is live band as well during dinner service, but we found it to be …MoreThis authentic Thai establishment is located at ground floor of The School, Jaya One. The restaurant is huge with stall-like concepts of all the dishes offered here. There is live band as well during dinner service, but we found it to be too noisy and intrusive for the diners. Maybe tweaking the volume or upgrading with a better sound system is recommended. Staff here is friendly, but we had some issue communicating well with the staff when ordering. But it was manageable. Ambiance was superb, not too hot eventhough it was packed with diners (efficient ventilation).The only issue we had with the food is the green curry chicken we ordered. Unfortunately, it was like green curry "soup" as it was very watery to our liking. But, the flavour is good and tasted delicious. Probably if the curry was creamier and thicker, it would have been perfect. Needed more chicken pieces as well. The star of the show must be the street fried Thai chicken wings and the Thai style deep fried fish with sweet & sour sauce. The fried chicken wings were fried to perfection and it was not too dry as well. Quite difficult to get deep fried chicken wings that are moist & tender. Bursting with flavour as well. The deep fried fish with sweet & sour sauce was excellent. Same as the deep fried chicken wings. The other dishes like the Tom yam, fried veggie surpassed our expectations as well. The Thai fish cakes were superb as well. Highly recommend to try.Dessert was good as well, recommend to have the red ruby. It was a really good complement after a superb meal. Mango with sticky rice was okay, but probably needed more of the coconut santan sauce. The pulut (sticky rice) was good. The taro iced and butterfly pea tea was fantastic as well. Pricing was decent and the food quality was fantastic. Recommended for big groups. Service was fast eventhough it was jam packed with diners.
Location: 100-G.001 Jaya One No. 72A Jalan Prof Diraja, Jln Profesor Diraja Ungku Aziz, Seksyen 13, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

So soft and tender that the pickiest eater of all couldn't stop eating it.◾San Jacobo RM28 - tender piece of pork sirloin filled with iberico ham and melted manchego cheese. My least favourite but credit to them, the meat was quite tender to begin with.◾ Pimentos asados con Arun (Ortiz) - marinated roasted pepper topped with tuna. For RM32, the soft and aromatic roasted pepper was topped with tuna and both combined well together.◾Valenciana paella RM37 - love the fact that I could order one portion, and that portion could easily feed 2-3 small eater.◾squid ink paella RM37◾juicy iberico pork ribs (half slab) at RM85 - fall-of-the-bone texture and well marinated pork ribs.. I couldn't stop munching on them! Paired perfectly with the red wine.◾Churros with chocolate RM17 - one of the most ordered dish in this restaurant. They have one section dedicated for this Spanish dessert.◾Basque cheese cake RM17 - although on the high side, their rendition of this by-accident dessert was flawless.◾cafe latte◾Sangria - there's this normal Sangria and then there's another one that made with champagne.If you think that the food is actually too much.. I had to clarify that I had gone there 3 times in a space of a month - 2 dinner and 1 coffee + cake sessions - just because I simply love most (if not all) of the dishes that I'd ordered. Coming here on weekends without reservation is not recommended unless you do not mind to wait.

Review: AVOID THIS PLACE.It was a decent experience... until we got the bill and realized our orders were …MoreAVOID THIS PLACE.It was a decent experience... until we got the bill and realized our orders were the wrong size.There was 3 ladies in our group. We eventually got our bill rectified (so kudos on that).What made our blood boil was that the server was mumbling loudly at the other side of the restaurant about how we wouldn't have ordered small to share. Worse still, he was mumbling (in Cantonese) "IF YOU DON'T HAVE MONEY THEN DON'T EAT HERE".Are you serious??? We do NOT appreciate being INSULTED. Food is mediocre and with servers like that? There's really NO reason why you should visit this restaurant.Opus, I really wanted to like you but no, never again.[Edit] P.S. I came across Opus again and am still bitter so I checked them out online. I realised they disallowed and removed the review section from their Facebook page after I posted the above there (this was a while back). High expectations of the owner's Vietnamese mother-in-law's cooking have only left heavy traces of MSG over beef pho noodles at a hefty RM18.00. Deservingly Vietnamese in name with the Thai basil, cilantro condiments and lime, but lacking in the generous beansprouts found in the best pho served by immigrant Vietnamese in Silicon Valley across the great ocean. Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Burnt cheesecake is made by the Basque country, particularly San Sebastian where it is said that a little incident by a baker in the kitchen led to the global sensation when the burnt cheesecake has taken the world over by storm. In …MoreBurnt cheesecake is made by the Basque country, particularly San Sebastian where it is said that a little incident by a baker in the kitchen led to the global sensation when the burnt cheesecake has taken the world over by storm. In Malaysia alone, many cafes and restaurants offer this dessert to those with sweet tooth. I have tried most of the places I'd known but the Japanese version in The Tokyo Restaurant, tucked on the 4th floor of Lot 10 KL.. remained elusive as I hardly go downtown.My opportunity came when I had to meet a customer in downtown KL one weekday and I utilised the time in between to give this place a try. There is a lift outside the mall that gives direct access to the 4th floor where many Japanese restaurants have set their foot here. Since it was a weekday afternoon, the place was almost empty so we could dine in peace.◾The whole restaurant setup was modern and tastefully decorated with warm ambience - perfect to kill some free time and to enjoy your food or dessert or even a cup of coffee◾They do serve limited food such as salad, sushi, burger, etc but since I was there for one thing only, I couldn't comment much on these.◾I ordered their famous burnt cheesecake - so famous that I could spot many Instagram featuring it. At RM20 per piece, it's probably the most expensive piece of cake I'd ever tried in my life. The cake was served lying down on the plate with a dollop of whipped cream on top. It was soft yet bold, with rich cheese taste that cheese lovers would appreciate, or else it would be too rich for general palates. It instantly melt as soon as it entered the mouth. Perhaps the whipped cream's purpose was to mellow down the cheesiness of the cake and it certainly did a good job at that.◾Iced latte did its job to satisfy my caffeine needs.. using premium coffee beans hence the premium price chargedAfter that we took a while to look around the refurbished Lot 10 - many establishments such as Sushi Azabu, Dashing Dining Says, etc... That I have not even stepped into yet. Time to discover more about it next time. For now.. it's a yes just to come and taste the famous burnt cheesecake.
Location: level 4 LOT 10 SHOPPING CENTER, 50, Jln Sultan Ismail, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Han Low
Review: Ordered the following for lunch:1) Beef Curry with add on Japanese style omelette2) Spiced Chicken c/w Rice …MoreOrdered the following for lunch:1) Beef Curry with add on Japanese style omelette2) Spiced Chicken c/w Rice3) Gateau Chocolate4) Add on Chamomile Tea & Iced Cafe LatteMiso soup:Served as part of the set lunch. The taste is not bad, fusion between the taste of miso with the starchy texture on Chinese-style shark-fin soup.Curry Beef with Rice:Japanese style curry, therefore on the sweet side. Taste is alright. The Japanese style omelette add-on tasted good, though not sure it justifies the RM 7 add on price. Portion of rice is normal/generous, but the portion of beef is very little. Served with a very odd green-coloured sauce on the side, which is very, very spicy and salty; did not bothered with the green sauce.Spiced Lemon Roasted Chicken:The texture of the roasted chicken is good, cooked quite close to perfection. Nonetheless, the "spiced" is very misleading; assumed that "spiced" in this sense would be on the lighter side (i.e. rosemary etc.) Turns out it's a lot of chili paste (a.k.a. sambal) on top of the chicken. The paste is too overwhelmingly spicy that the chicken can be barely tasted. Mixed vegetables and rice served together, the tiny potato is good, whereas the mixture of vegetables are so-so. The Ramen-style egg (Ajitsuke Tamago) is very good.Gateau Chocolate:The chocolate within the cake tasted okay, bittersweet. Cake is a bit on the dry side. Served with sweetened whipped cream (a little too sweet).Drinks:Chamomile Tea & Iced Cafe Cafe were both good and acceptable quality. Happy with the drinks.Service:Service is overall satisfactory. Staff tend to be poorly coordinated, but the number of staff of duty makes up for it. If members of staff are properly trained or if there is any good system established, less number of staff would be required.Ambiance:Cozy and somewhat comfortable (came during a time which is less busy). Tend to be crowded on weekends for late-lunches and dinner time.Total cost of meal is about RM 90. Personally a little disappointed (went in with high hopes). Would not say it is good value for money as the food were not up to expectations.

Author: lmt6618 *
Review: A fushion of Thai chef & a Malaysian offering authentic Thai @ reasonably price. Our Thai lady chef is meticulous in her ingredients which transform into beautifully flavoured & cooked Thai food. Thai loves sweetness in their food, however …MoreA fushion of Thai chef & a Malaysian offering authentic Thai @ reasonably price. Our Thai lady chef is meticulous in her ingredients which transform into beautifully flavoured & cooked Thai food. Thai loves sweetness in their food, however our Chef is light on sugar enough to bring the aroma and original Thai home cooked food. Try their reasonably priced set lunch & you get an intro of the main menu. The gravy is thick, thick coconut milk in harmony with its spices (Green & Red curry & spicy pork). The broad 3" by 0.5cm flat pork skewer (similar to stay) is a must try. It looks big n thick (40% fat + 60% meat) but melts in your mouth. Do plan to come early and it may be busy during weekends. You can savour your Thai food cravings here & save rm20 new exit tax :)

Author: Ch Wo
Review: Review is based on the fact that the waiter was so adamant that most dishes had no sugar or could have sugar taken out or that the coconut shake  wasn't very sweet as we were trying to accommodate diabetics. …MoreReview is based on the fact that the waiter was so adamant that most dishes had no sugar or could have sugar taken out or that the coconut shake  wasn't very sweet as we were trying to accommodate diabetics.Coconut shake was clearly not devoid of sugar even though I asked for no added sugar. Red snapper with Chili lime sauce was definitely balanced with sugar. Pad Thai tasted sweet. This is all fine but when you ask for no sugar and he claims to accommodate you but you also get the feeling you can't trust him, that really gives you a bad taste in the mouth.To top it off, Saturday evening at 6pm and they are out of green tea. Really? No tea to be had and almost all drinks have sugar in them.As far as food goes, they had no salt grilled tilapia. The red snapper is quite good with the Chili lime. Pad Thai is fine and well cooked. Fried chicken skin didn't feel like it was freshly fried as it was not piping hot and  you can always tell as it was not super crunchy. Fish cakes are spicy and quite good. Overall, I expected better so early into dinner service. The only reason why it is 2 stars and not 3 is because the waiter was being helpful when in fact, he didn't even bother to try. Not wanting to eat sugar is not just a health choice but life and death for some people. Please let them know that.

Author: leon j
Review: Saturday nights without a reservation may be iffy and we waited about 25 minutes for a table for 2. The place was packed to the rafters. Kudos to the …MoreSaturday nights without a reservation may be iffy and we waited about 25 minutes for a table for 2. The place was packed to the rafters. Brightly lit, with well-spaced out tables, Baan Rao is very tastefully put together. Kudos to the owners. And from the exterior it looks enticing.We got the Tom Yam seafood, the Prawn in chilli paste, Som Tam, Tako, Red Ruby, Kedongdong juice and Lemongrass juice. The tom yam was good (although my other half thought it could have been better). We agreed that the Prawn and Som Tam was excellent. I especially like the Kedongdong juice. Piquant, tangy and delightfully appetizing. The Tako was ok but the Red Ruby was disappointing. The ice was coarse making it impossible to chew. They also ran out of nangka and replaced it with "peaches" which was ridiculous. And of course the peaches were bad!Service however was excellent even though it was packed. I especially like how "Ah Lun" kept the waiting crowd at ease and how he managed the place. Kudos to him. Pricing is very fair.Baan Tao could easily deserve 5 stars but the dessert took them down a notch. But I'm sure I will be back again soon.

Review: Have been here multiple times and so far I haven’t been disappointed!Decided to try their omakase this round and it was surprisingly decent. I mean for the price you’re paying - it’s worth it as you won’t be disappointed with the …MoreHave been here multiple times and so far I haven’t been disappointed!Decided to try their omakase this round and it was surprisingly decent. I mean for the price you’re paying - it’s worth it as you won’t be disappointed with the taste.There weren’t many sashimi in our 9-course meal but the cooked food was really different.My personal favourite is the duck foie gras. It has a Smokey taste and I was so reluctant to take my last bite because I wanted the taste to linger in my mouth!Their tofu appetiser had the century egg filling on top and it went really really well together.The sashimi and seafood was fresh - tho the cuts weren’t the best but it was still enjoyable.The only thing we didn’t like was the fried fish and scallop soup right before we got our dessert. Fish was dry and scallop soup had the mala peppery taste, which was too unusual to my liking.The dessert? Well you can never go wrong with yuzu ice cream after all the heavy flavours.The restaurant is very comfortable too and the service was good! Perfect for any kinds of occasion.
Location: 2nd Floor, No 22A, 1, Jalan 17/54, Section 17, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Review: Uroko has firmly established themselves as one of the top Japanese restaurants in PJ. Come any day and they are quite packed - worse when it comes to weekends. Come any day and they are quite packed - worse when it comes to weekends. It is impossible to get a table without reservation on weekends. Book their private room way in advance for more intimate affair.The restaurant is dimly lit yet exudes the aura of calmness as I entered the premise. The service team is very fast to bring you to the table and a thick menu book with be given to you - set menu (lunch or dinner) is available too. You can choose to sit at the sushi counter and watch as the chef prepares your order. Oh yes! If you're feeling adventurous, go for their omakase where the chef will prepare the freshest ingredients to you on the spot.◾They are well-stocked on Japanese spirit and sometimes they will have promotion on certain sake(s). Have it cold or hot depending on your mood.◾Nothing beats a bowl of fresh salad to whet the appetite - my favourite will be salmon ball salad where they use raw salmon slices to wrap around the fresh salad like a ball, with ponzu-like sauce as dressing; and◾Uroko salad - soft shell crab & crispy salmon skin on top of the salad, with sesame mayo sauce dressing. This is good too!◾ If you like sashimi, there's a high chance that you'll like uni (sea urchin)... Fresh with umami-goodness◾Unagi kabayaki - I took risk by ordering the grilled eel and it paid off - it was very good without the muddy taste. I cleaned the plate◾boiled salmon soup◾take note that they have what they called "Lady Set" that comes with a plate of sashimi, set of sushi, salad, chawanmushi and rice.. I'd say it's value for money◾ The selection for dinner set was quite good and there must be something that fit your requirement◾ Desserts... Go for their awesome yuzu, goma and matcha ice cream.Leo's verdict - Uroko has become a favourite destination for me and my family to eat fine Japanese food. It ticks all the right boxes - fresh ingredients, comfortable settings and close to home.
Location: 2nd Floor, No 22A, 1, Jalan 17/54, Section 17, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Alan
Review: I am a sucker for beautifully designed spaces that offers great food. Uroko embodies all that and has quickly elevated itself to my favourite place for dining. …MoreI am a sucker for beautifully designed spaces that offers great food. Uroko embodies all that and has quickly elevated itself to my favourite place for dining.Uroko is located on the second floor of a corner shop lot in fashionable S17, Petaling Jaya. The restaurant itself is actually quite spacious, with a dining area that currently sits 28 (CMCO), a sushi bar area that sits 5 and there is 2 private rooms. Not forgetting, they also have a sake bar.The interior is beautiful. The space is fitted with custom made furnitures that is both beautiful and comfortable. The lighting is appropriately dimmed to create a cozy environment. The wall is fitted with gold matted fixtures adding a touch of class and sophistication to the space.But a beautiful interior is not the only thing.The food is delicious, beautifully presented and the quality is exceptional. The menu is filled with a range Japanese favourites. However, the real gems in the menu are dishes that have been infused with creative twists. I spotted a dish infused with foie gras and a carpaccio inspired dish in the menu.Our starter, the Salmon Carpaccio was extremely flavourful and colourful.The salad was visually appetising with its vibrant array of colour (Salmon dusted with truffles paired with crunchy greens), taste and textures.The Mars Maki was another delightful taste sensation combining a frittered spicy maki (did they add a hint of chilli padi into the maki?) with eel and tobiko.Our last dish was the Take Sushi platter. It came with 3 pieces of Uramaki and 6 different Nigiri Sushi plated from the lightest to the smokiest, left to the right.Sadly, one thing in the menu we did not get to try today, was the their Japan Amera Tomato. It costs RM35 a pop and I heard that it was divine.

Hence repeated clientele is the strongest and best term to describe this place.You start by having breakfast with two half boiled eggs with roti-bakar and a cup of tea or coffee from the anchor owner who only serves drinks and some tidy bits. It a family owned anchor with siblings as cashier , preparing beverages and serving the customers.As for brunch and lunch you have other sub hawkers with a medley of chicken chops, spaghetti  Bolognese, Carbonara and  Oglio Aglio. Bakuteh and various noodle soups and rice -both fried and porridge- with a selection of fish, vegetables , seafood and meat dishes to choose from.A mixture of Western and Oriental Chinese cuisines at prices the layman can afford.Dinner has the same choice but one have to be there at 7pm to enjoy the full range of dishes to select from.As for desserts you have the typical Chinese cakes and Pows- lotus seeds, chicken or meats- to relished from..Soft liquors and various makes of beers are served for those who likes to finish off with some hard knocks.A truly awesome and Delightful place for the home away from home diners and daily stopover for any meals of the day.You can bring your own special brand of Chinese tea as a bonus. It will be served in teapots and small cups to complete the ambience of  " August Tea Garden ".A place to visit for you daily meals at prices that suit every one's pockets.Truly Malaysians of Chinese Ethnic origin.😊😋😋😋😊😉😴

Author: Azril Annuar
Review: Went there to celebrate my mother in law's birthday during the CMCO. The guys there diligently follow the SOPs but that did not affect their service in any way as everything was utterly immaculate. …MoreWent there to celebrate my mother in law's birthday during the CMCO. The guys there diligently follow the SOPs but that did not affect their service in any way as everything was utterly immaculate.The owner, Carmine, is an extremely friendly and affable guy who regaled us with tales of his hometown in Naples and his little quest to bring authentic Naples cuisine to Malaysia.We started with two appetisers: the eggplant parmigiana as well as the deep fried calamari and prawns. Both were fantastic.Then we sampled the margharita pizza. The blend of tomato sauce and mozzarella, on top of a perfectly baked pizza dough was divine. Unfortunately because of Covid-19 and the logistical disruption from Italy, we could not sample the buffalo mozzarella for the pizza.Based on Carmine's recommendation we ordered the penne de genovese, which is penne covered in beef and onion stew. The beef was super tender and the sauce went perfectly with the pasta. I highly recommend it as Carmine said it's the only place in Klang Valley that offers it on the menu.As I am on a quest to find the best Arabiatta, I ordered the penne arabiatta. It is good but I think there's room for improvement. But then again, maybe I am biased towards the arabiatta I tasted when I was on a cruise.Carmine, who is a professionally trained engineer, also entertained us as it is obvious he is great at conversation. After being in Malaysia for probably more than 18 years, he is very well versed with local current events.During our chat, it was clear to us he also has good knowledge on local cuisines. The jovial Italian also surprisingly shared his recipe for the penne de genovese with my mother in law, who cheekily asked him how to make it as a birthday present.All in all, I highly recommend it. I am going to go there again and I plan on spreading his restaurant by word of mouth as he told me his business has been badly hit by Covid-19 and revenue was down by 70 per cent.I. Do. Not. Want. This. Place. To. Shutter. Down.If anyone wants to have authentic Italian cuisine from Naples, this is it. Ciao!
Location: Hartamas Shopping Centre, M-1-1, Sri Hartamas, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Having a good western meal need not to be an expensive affair. I remember the good old days when eating western meal used to be affordable, but soon it's getting higher and higher due to inflation and increased standard of living.First time I read about Habanna was when a close blogger friend wrote about it, and then Cheah, my close makan and whisky kaki mentioned about this place. When he talks, I listen because I trust his taste. And they get their beef supply from another friend who is a fine food importer.◾Armed with a bottle of Shiraz, cabernet sauvignon and cabernet Franc blend... We started our dinner in good mood.◾The son requested for a chicken burger - no regret as the sight of him gobbling up the whole burger made me hungrier. Served with fries and bacon on the side. Priced at RM16.90, it was almost a steal◾garlic pork (RM9.80) - essentially a side order but it came with generous portion. The smell of garlic was heavenly as it enveloped the pork belly - the girls love it and they finished it quickly which was a surprise as both of them normally eat very slow◾Charbroiled Apple Belly - Jenn commented that the pork belly was quite bland without the apple dipping sauce (hence the pairing of both) but on the bright side, the pork belly has that melt-in-the-mouth texture. RM19.90 well paid◾The Three Amigos (RM24.90) - it came highly recommended by the waitress and surely it didn't disappoint.. three succulent chicken thigh (hence the name) grilled perfectly and glazed with their house BBQ sauce.. to me it was almost perfect combination. Served with wedges and salad, I normally prefer pork but this dish got me in love with poultry once again!Do not expect fancy and extravagant design - everything is kept simple including the menu and price that will not burn a hole in your pocket. For the quality of food that they serve, I'd say it's best bang for your buck.Note: Corkage charge is very friendly at RM2 per person (yes you didn't read it wrong) so feel free to bring your favourite wine.

I then informed the owner and his immediate response was, "Oh you should have ordered the Duroc cut instead if you want something more tender. Didn't my daughter suggest this to you?"Umm, this is not a suitable response at all. Firstly, belly cut can be perfectly tender IF you cook the fat slowly and properly, which is the chef's responsibility. Secondly, no one told me about this other cut (it's not listed on the menu) so what's the point of bringing it up now? Moreover, he's just looking for someone else to blame, including the customer.So i just politely asked him to please cook it longer for me and he took it back to the kitchen. After about 15 minutes, he gave me a new serving, which isn't what I expected. But he said, "Not to worry, I won't charge you for the earlier piece. Hope you enjoy this Duroc cut" which was confusing cuz I never asked him to change the type of cut and he never told me what cut this was? But I was hungry so I ate it, assuming he would maintain the same price.Guess what? Shock #1 is that the second belly was only slightly less chewy and undercooked than the first. Sigh, I wanted to complain again but we were running late. So I just cut off the fat (which is my fave part if cooked well) and ate what I could.But Shock #2 came when we paid. The original dish I ordered was RM19.90 and yet I was charged RM29.90 without being informed at all. It's only when I checked the bill against the menu price and I asked the waitress, then she casually says, "Oh the Duroc is a more expensive cut".How is this acceptable? They have a responsibility to inform me about a change in price and only if I agree can they then give me a pricier piece. Otherwise just cook the original piece as intended.Such a lousy place, don't waste your time here. Oh, and the pork burger was dry and much smaller than the bun.

Author: Joon Ong
Review: About Menya Shi Shi Do:Mainly sells ramen in Tonkotsu broth (pork bone soup). There's green onion, black fungus, Japanese soft boiled egg and Char Siew (Roasted Pork slice) in the …MoreAbout Menya Shi Shi Do:Mainly sells ramen in Tonkotsu broth (pork bone soup). There's green onion, black fungus, Japanese soft boiled egg and Char Siew (Roasted Pork slice) in the ramen. It has different soup flavours such as soy sauce, basil, curry and etc. You can also combine up to 3 flavours in a bowl of ramen. Not to forget it has some special ramen such as Aka Oni (extra spicy ramen), iipon Yaki Buta Tsukemen (big slab of roasted pork) ramen.About the environment:The design are pretty Japanese authentic with red lantern and comic book pages on the wall. Seats are... ehm normal wooden seats you can get from Ikea. Do expect a long queue during peak hour. The distance between seats are far enough during covid-19 pandemic.About the dish:The soup is smooth and mildly rich with sweet flavour of pork bone, slightly smooth texture of collagen. Noodle is chewy and absorbed the taste of the soup enough to be flavourful. Japanese soft boiled egg has runny york which is good but the outer egg doesn't have enough flavour, as if the egg is not marinate long enough by looking at the colour. Black fungus are crunchy and flavourful itself and with the soup. Char Siew is thin and rich in flavour, the saltiness makes it stands out from the soup in a good way. The fat level of Char Siew is low but still very easy to chew.Conclusion:I love the richness of the soup where you can still finish the whole bowl without feeling greasy. With RM22-26 a bowl, it is a reasonable price and I would love to revisit and try some of their special ramen. 4-4.5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐

Author: Takyaa
Review: One of, if not the best Ramen in town!They serve all-tonkotsu soup base with multiple choices of flavors, the soup is …MoreOne of, if not the best Ramen in town!They serve all-tonkotsu soup base with multiple choices of flavors, the soup is creamy and rich, while being fresh without pork smell! (There were some ramen joints that serves decent tonkotsu pork soup as well but i personally didn't liked the pork smell or the excessive presence of oil within it)The noodle texture is al-Dante, if you're planning to take picture before eating, i would suggest ordering hard/firm noodle so you can have longer waiting time before you eat it without being worry of noodle texture being overcook/ too soft.Their soup flavor choices are divided into single, double, and triple flavor. Their single and double flavor soup base is "drinking friendly" for those who likes to do so because they aren't that oily compared to some other ramen joints' soup base. However, for the triple flavor soup, it can be thicker and harder to drink for certain people! So, be sure to ask for flavor recommendation based on your preference when you order!Also, one of the biggest impact i received from the ramen here was the Pork shoulder. It is definitely the best one i've had before. The flavor was mind-blowing, just like a taste bomb, impact-fully explodes in your mouth, spreading flavor that matches well with the ramen while leaving a satisfying after taste. Therefore i recommend ordering their Shi shi ramen for 2 pieces of them!Lastly, the price is affordable & much cheaper than many other ramen restaurants like Ippudo or bankara. Not to mention that the taste is far more superior! (subjectively speaking). It made sense why people willing to queue for half to an hour for the ramen, but i would suggest going for the dine in for best experience during off peak or weekdays so you can have more time to enjoy the ramen!

Review: What's your favourite Italian restaurant? Honestly for me, Italian restaurant is not authentic Italian without pork (this sentiment is also echoed by most of my makan Kaki). That's why my favourite remains Verona, Sapore & Neroteca - just …MoreWhat's your favourite Italian restaurant? Honestly for me, Italian restaurant is not authentic Italian without pork (this sentiment is also echoed by most of my makan Kaki). That's why my favourite remains Verona, Sapore & Neroteca - just to name a few!However if there's one Italian that doesn't serve pork, yet I still go back from time to time.. it'd be La Risata. Something about this restaurant that makes me keep coming back - and it's their consistency and value pricing of their food.◾Zuppe Di Pesce (seafood soup) - available in half or full serving, I always go for the former as it's big enough to serve 2-3 person. It is actually a herb-spiced tomato broth served in a rather big bowl, filled generously with seafoods such as mussels, fish chunks, clams, prawns and squids. Did I mention that they spiced up the broth using bird eye chilly? It's a touch of genius I'd say, given that I love eating my chilly.◾Funghi alla Griglia or their grilled fresh champignon mushrooms with garlic. Gotta love the earthy taste of this dish.◾Pizza Margherita - featuring tomato, mozzarella, oregano and basil, nothing beats classic Italian style pizza done right.◾Agnello alla Griglia RM59 - grilled Australian lamb loin with fennel and black pepper crust, served with mashed chickpea & vegetable capitans finished with a red wine reduction. One of my favourite dishes in this restaurant - just the loin and the sauce, I don't know how to appreciate chickpea mash. Lol◾ spaghetti alle Vongole - the awesome pasta was cooked with clams in garlic, chilly and white wine sauce.◾ Spaghetti Alla Risata - a house specialty, imagine a hearty mixed seafood in hearty spicy tomato sauce... Baked in aluminium foil. Taste-wise similar to the seafood soup but with addition of spaghetti.◾ House Wines by the glass are available or if you're in the mood, go for the bottle.Instead of a fine dining eatery, it is in fact a rustic and casual Italian restaurant patronised mostly by locals. Coming here without any reservation on weekends is almost impossible so be smart and call ahead ya. To me, it's a money well spent especially when I get to eat quality food like these.

Author: Viktor Tey
Review: My second experience at this restaurant was a mixed bag, leaving much to be desired. …MoreMy second experience at this restaurant was a mixed bag, leaving much to be desired.The mushroom soup was a primary source of cognitive dissonance—there is no cream in it, nor any discernible seasoning.  The soup was not strained, leaving bits of mushroom removed of any valuable texture or taste.The bread in accompaniment was by stark contrast. Absolutely delicious and thoughtfully toasted.We enjoyed the headliner Spanish Spare Ribs which though generous in portion and taste, was still less than tender. It was also served with an overly sweet sauce, which overshadows the meat.Service overall was timely—but we were served one soup at a time, leading to an awkward wait in between.I enjoyed the pasta aglio olio with bacon, though I recommend reducing the amount of chili seeds in the meal as it is disruptive to both chewing and swallowing.Overall, for the price, it was a very middling experience. More of a novelty than a staple. Quite a pity as the venue itself has a great ambiance which exceeds its cuisine.And finally—it is indeed true that only cash is accepted here. Truly unusual for a meal that usually ends in three digits or more. There's no ATM or bank within walking distance so if you're carrying a light wallet... Keep walking.

We ordered the Jamon Iberico platter to share followed with the Pork Ribs in Mesquite BBQ sauce. We finished the meal with a Chocolate Lava cake.Each dish was very tasty and satisfying. The Iberico Ham platter came with plenty of ham, sliced at just the right thickness to enjoy. Not too sweet or heavy and came with a serving of vanilla ice cream topped with salted caramel sauce.Definitely a great place for a romantic dinner or as a treat with friends. Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: Mediterranean dishes at its best!As I passed by this restaurant everytime after I finished having my coffee at …MoreMediterranean dishes at its best!As I passed by this restaurant everytime after I finished having my coffee at Cream nearby, I recalled on a Mediterranean restaurant that I used to go in Mont Kiara a long time ago. A quick check confirmed that they have moved to Dataran Prima in PJ.Wondering how they have changed after all these years, I made a reservation for dinner one Saturday evening. While it was almost impossible to find a parking here on normal working days, it's almost deserted come evening and weekends.Striking a casual yet cosy atmosphere, the waiters made our visit welcome by their higher-than-average service. Armed with a bottle of Spanish Tempranillo, the evening has just got better.◾sous vide white pork ribs - it felt like Chinese style braised pork ribs but delicious nonetheless.◾smoked chicken croquettes - served lollipop style. I just picked up the skewer and took one whole ball into the mouth.◾bacon & melted mozzarella sandwich with semi-dried tomatoes - visually striking and inviting, most probably due to the bacon on a bed of melted cheese on top of the crusty, crunchy yet light sourdough bread. Fold and eat away. Served with a bowl of fries.◾Basic pasta - penne in pesto sauce without any topping at RM24. The daughter declared that the pesto sauce was one of the best she'd ever tried.◾Margarita pizza - RM30.. initially thinking how on earth were we going to finish the pizza given that we'd ordered so many items, we somehow managed to finish the delicious and competently prepared pizza. The crust was simply lovely in texture.◾Seafood risotto with semi-dried tomato sauce - at RM42, this was the most expensive risotto in the menu◾Pan seared foie gras - by far the most expensive dish of the evening at RM82 for 50g liver. A rather big piece of foie gras perfectly cooked served on a bed of salad. Honestly it was not enough for both of us.By the end of the dinner, all of us agreed that this place deserved to be in my permanent to-go list.
Location: Menara Prima, B-G-17 Tower B Entrance, Jalan PJU 1/39, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Review: Originate from KL, Hokkien mee is liked by many people and thats include my friends from HK and Japan. Damansara Uptown Hokkien mee has been operating …MoreOriginate from KL, Hokkien mee is liked by many people and thats include my friends from HK and Japan. There are many Hokkien mee stores in Klang Valley and everyone have their own preference. Damansara Uptown Hokkien mee has been operating here for more than 20 years and I've been visiting them while they have tables on the road sides. They have done quite a massive upgrade now and occupied 3 shoplots. Their Hokkien mee is still pretty good and full of flavor. The ingredients includes lean pork, prawns, cabbage and lots of pork lard but its missing another ingredient that I love - pork liver. Besides Hokkien mee, they of course serve the other fried noodles like Cantonese style kuey teow, yuan yang, lor mee and fried rice. I would usually order a bowl of pork soup to pair with the noodles, however I found the soup is less peppery now. But overall still a good place to go for a nice plate of Hokkien mee!

The only drawback is that the skin is not crispy. For the duck, you must go early cause they run out of duck around 8.30pm on peak day.

Author: Mr. J
Review: I'm not a big fan of fish and chips, but I loved the food at this restaurant. The owner was raised in England by his Malaysian mother and he was disappointed that he couldn't find "proper" fish and chips here, which is why he decided to …MoreI'm not a big fan of fish and chips, but I loved the food at this restaurant. The owner was raised in England by his Malaysian mother and he was disappointed that he couldn't find "proper" fish and chips here, which is why he decided to open this shop and offer authentic fish and chips. I've never been to the UK so I can't comment on the authenticity, but the food here was really good. You have a selection of fish and batters that you can mix and match with a selection of sides to choose from. The fish was excellent, brilliantly cooked in the batter. Chips were amazing, as was the tartar sauce. No complaints about the food at all. The prices are quite expensive, but the portion sizes and the food quality go some way to justifying the price. The shop isn't certified halal, but the ingredients are all from halal suppliers and there's no pork products or alcohol in any of the cooking. No beer in the batter either. GrabPay is an option for those looking for cashless transactions. I'll definitely come back if I have the chance.

Author: Izrin Muaz Md Adnan
Review: This is a review based on a dining experience on Thursday 8 April 2021. First of all, the decor. I would have preferred a classy decor with vague Indian furnishings and faux Mughal paintings. Instead what you get is a decor quite similar to …MoreThis is a review based on a dining experience on Thursday 8 April 2021. First of all, the decor. I would have preferred a classy decor with vague Indian furnishings and faux Mughal paintings. Instead what you get is a decor quite similar to Pizza Hut. Enough said. Anybody sceptical should go in and see for himself. We ordered the kurma Zafar Shahi, paneer Shahi and chicken biryani. The kurma was way too sweet and diluted; the beef was tough, was obviously not fresh and not even cooked properly. It seemed to have come out straight from the fridge and dropped into the kurma. I got the shock of my life when I tasted this since it was touted the house speciality. This was a dish made for Bahadur Shah Zafar; I can't imagine the last Mughal emperor wanting to eat this muck. If it was served to him, the cook probably wouldn't even be alive by dawn the next day. The Shahi Paneer was obviously made using the same spice mixture as the kurma Zafar Shahi. Again this was unexpectedly sweet and diluted, watery. It was edible but unremarkable by any standard. The chicken biryani was equally rotten. In fact the chicken meat wasn't cooked properly and was even a little raw. On top of it, it didn't taste fresh. After our impressive experience at the SS15 D'tandoor, this was a major letdown. A pity, because this was supposed to have been the original joint. Obviously standards are different here. The service was on the brusque side, hardly welcoming. After serving the most appalling dishes and having us pay for it, they didn't even have the courtesy of opening the door and wishing us good night. I should add that we didn't finish the food that night. Our appetite had been spoilt by the ghastly experience. I should add also that food took a while to be served, presumably because they were too busy with delivery orders. This place has mixed reviews; in fact, most of the reviews were decidedly negative. Our experience dining here simply confirms what the rest of the customers feel about this place. This is a total rip off and a waste of time. Just stay away from this place, at least until they brush up their act. The way the waiter who took our order treated/eyed us was as if we couldn't afford to pay or that they were doing us a great favour in admitting us. And all this to partake of a meal so abominable that I have not been able to write about it a good many weeks after the horrifying experience. Just do your palette a favour and keep well away from this joint.
Location: 52, Jalan SS 21/62, Damansara Utama, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

Author: Nipun C
Review: Absolutely delicious curries and food. Very rarely you'll find a banana leaf rice shop that serves mint, coconut and ginger chutney with achaar as part of a banana leaf set. Their speciality is the yoghurt curry(give it a go) I enjoyed …MoreAbsolutely delicious curries and food. Very rarely you'll find a banana leaf rice shop that serves mint, coconut and ginger chutney with achaar as part of a banana leaf set. Their speciality is the yoghurt curry(give it a go) I enjoyed their mutton curry. Thick, spicy, masala-fied, exactly what an Indian curry should be. Their assorted vegetables were tasty as well with green vege, beans, potato masala (4 varieties of veges). The icing on the cake is the kesari that comes along, just the right sweetness, just the right amount.3 of us had 3 BLR sets with 3 side dishes (chicken perattal, mutton varuval and chicken 65) 1 watermelon juice, 2 limau ais and we paid RM64, a decent average of Rm21 per person for BLR,drinks and 3 dishes. The "annes" they're are very kind and polite, ever ready to serve with such a humbling manner that many restaurants lack.Try catching a spot under the big shady trees just outside of the restaurant (watch out for falling leaves and twigs) all in all it was a superb lunch for me and my friends8
Location: 4, Jalan 1/3, Seksyen 1, Petaling Jaya, Selangor

My favourite ones are the tofu cheese & hojicha cake, amongst the other more typical but equally good ones like the oreo mille crepes etc. Coffees, also good!Onto the food, you can still order the basic pastas that they used to have on the menu, just request it from the waiter. Their bolognese ham pastas are my favourite with the carbonara salmon. Cheese baked black rice is also one of my favourites.I've graduated and am moving away, but this cafe will be setting a very high standard for any other cafe to live up to it lol. Cafe ambience is nice too of course, great for anyone to come. Only thing is of course seating is limited, so come earlier. Really hope they do even better and can expand their business even more! Thank you After Black for years of good food and good memories.

Review: Mithun Mohan's Thosai Cafe (The Curve, PJ) which serves 82 different varieties of thosai (yup, read that as dosa), with a flamboyant flair typical of a music festival. …MoreMithun Mohan's Thosai Cafe (The Curve, PJ) which serves 82 different varieties of thosai (yup, read that as dosa), with a flamboyant flair typical of a music festival.The band at the courtyard of The Curve was thriking notes of the blues, and old school classics,  as warm Badam Milk (rich with almonds, cashew and pista), and hot Masala Chai hit all the nostalgic nerve spots.  Mithun's thosai, each one crisp (he doesn't use rice flour but semolina batter), fresh veggies including beetroot (I love beetroot), with secret spices flown from India.A former ITian from Bangalore, India,  who landed in Malaysia, Mithun's beer and thosai parties at home became such a hit, that prompted a stint with a hospitality brand,  and eventually the idea of an open diner churning out home thosai from South India.The popular local vote?  The Dil Khush Thosai  (Happy Heart) with a beautiful backstory to it.Mithun can tell you this in person.I had a beautiful conversation and musical evening  ❤ Go with friends and family #TheStilettoFoodie #EthelDaCosta

Review: Have you ever wondered what the hype was all about after visiting a restaurant? That's how I felt after eating at Tiffin's. That's how I felt after eating at Tiffin's. A 4.4 rating is pretty impressive by today's standards so I figured I must try the food. Although the food was not bad it was also not impressive. We had the pork neck with rice and pork noodles in broth set. The broth was quite good but the pork lard was rancid - chef please taste it before you throw it in the broth. The pork neck was in the words of a MKR contestant just "meh". For dessert, we had mango with sticky rice and for $12.80 a plate they could have served sweeter mangoes. The one thing I truly enjoyed was the Thai Milk Tea. Last words - don't visit Tiffin's with high expectations, you may be disappointed 😉

As I dipped them in the chocolate syrup and put them in my mouth, I just saw the number of defeated churros from other eateries I had. I would return again and again for this churros where i never returned for any other churros i had before. The total experience was marvelous. Surely there is more space for perfection. The mushroom gravy given is a big No, watery & rather bland. Steak not well marinated & not succulent. So, not meet my liking. Order ice-mocha which I think this ice mocha is more like made from 3in1, it’s not from coffee brewing machine definitely. There are room for improvement. Staffs are actually helpful. They are very willing to help you take photo whenever you request. But, after we hv make the payment & walked out, suddenly another staff come after us & asked whether we hv ald pay the bill. This is really a drawback. Staff shall check the POS whether the table hv been closed & make appropriate SOP in place to avoid misunderstanding on the billing matter.

Review: I came here for both lunch and dinner on different occasions, honestly this place is overpriced. The pasta buffet is especially disappointing as they serve you a plate full of pastas with barely any quality ingredients on it (e.g. smoked …MoreI came here for both lunch and dinner on different occasions, honestly this place is overpriced. The pasta buffet is especially disappointing as they serve you a plate full of pastas with barely any quality ingredients on it (e.g. smoked duck pasta with only 1 piece of smoked duck, fish pasta with 2 small pieces of frozen dolly fish, pesto pasta with dark murky green unappetizing pesto sauce, aglio olio with pasta drenched in cheap olive oil etc). All the other refillable side dishes are subpar, something like romaine lettuce salad, canned soup and Wall's ice-cream. That's pretty underwhelming for a RM39.90 buffet. Dinner wise, their main dish starts somewhere around RM40 and all the way to RM100+. The food is more decent at night but don't forget the premium that you're paying. Ordering seafood platter here is a play of russian roulette as the seafood is not always fresh (like 2/4 prawns are not fresh, fish smells fishy). Meat dishes are better, harder to go wrong I suppose.This is a quiet place with good view overlooking the lake and some housing area with a bit of greenery. It's a good place to sit and talk for the entire afternoon/night and no worries about parking space as it is located at a sort-of abandoned plaza. However when compared to similar Western food places with more or less the same price tag, the food here isn't that impressive. I'd recommend those who like a bit of privacy and fancy themselves some good lake view for dinner here, not so much for the lunch buffet.
Restaurant: Secret Of Louisiana at the lake

I ordered the beef steak which i would rate is Okok only nothing special about it. Overall rating for the food was 4/10.Lastly, the dessert came and i believe that was the best tasting compared to everything else. Didnt take a photo of the dessert as it was a total disappointment already and I was rushing to get the hell out of here. My girlfriend wasnt enjoying herself. 6/10 for the dessert.Conclusion is for the price over RM 400 I believe I could get way better food then this.To be fair I will give this place 1 more chance as I would go back during lunch hour for their lunch meals. Many friends told me the food is actually good but they have the worst services ever. Staff didnt know what they are doing. I surely will return on a less crowded event for lunch or a simple dinner just to give the food 1 more go. If is disappointing, sorry to the secret of Louisiana it will be the last.

Review: Reliability Is The Inevitable By-product of SimplicityFirst off, this is a review of their food delivery and not dine-in. …MoreReliability Is The Inevitable By-product of SimplicityFirst off, this is a review of their food delivery and not dine-in.We are no stranger to this restaurant which is our go-to for simple and value for money meal. The Hamburg steak was cook perfectly with a slight tinge of pink on the inside but nicely charred on the edges. Topped with an egg and some vegetables giving the dish some colour.Recommended? Although every once in a while we do enjoy surprises, most of the time, we would choose a safer and predictable meal knowing we won’t go hungry over a fancy looking meal that could go very wrongOur full review is on Instagram & YouTube ( @monk3yseendo )

Cannoli: Shell was abit hard for me to bite afraid it will break my braces. But the ricotta cream was light and not sweet, exactly how I like it to be! Both mango and chocolate flavors are good!6. Christmas bon bon: It's actually pumpkin spice chocolate, this one quite sweet but very cute! 😍7. Focaccia: This truffle butter tastes amazing and goes very well with the warm buns   This place easily beat any of those overpriced establishments in KL. I will not hesitate to recommend this place to anyone and will definitely visit again!! ❤️

The staff surprised us (at no extra charge) with tiny cake samples for my friend's birthday, with a piped Happy Birthday message on the plate - - a nice thoughtful detail! Wine is available, by the glass; champagne by the bottle only. It was very quiet on the Sunday night we were there, which allowed for an intimate atmosphere. I strongly recommend we keep these clever and hardworking restaurateurs in business!

The cultured butter wasn't interesting …MoreI am not sure if I was unlucky or other reviewers doesn't know what good food taste like. Today's dinner was extremely underwhelming. The items were as follow: Complimentary bread and snack of the day. The cultured butter wasn't interesting according to both myself and my dinner partner. It was butter with gula melaka and cheese shaved on it if i was not mistaken. To be able to screw up something as simple as complimentary bread is just impressive. To be fair it probably wasn't up to our taste buds. As for the appetizer, we had the mussel soup and cold salmon. The cold salmon very very appetizing but I can't say the same for the mussels. It was like baby's puke to be honest. I did not enjoy the soup at all. I haven't had lunch today, the only reason i finish the bowl was because I was really hungry, beggars can't be chooser but I think if there was a choice a beggar wouldn't finish the bowl of soup.Moving on, it was the main dish,  we ordered the quail risotto and grilled pork belly. To quote Gordon Ramsay: "the risotto was like baby food, it's mush". Calling yourself and italian restaurant but serving that level of risotto is just an outright embarrassment. On the bright side, the quail was at least decent. Then the pork belly, it was just meh, it was serve with a bunch of random stuff just to fill out the plate. How do you over salt your spinach and giving me a vege that tastes like just salt marinated in vege? Don't the chef do QC before serving? If they do, the chef is hopeless. Overall, the main dish is at best a 1 star for the quail. We also ordered the pasta with smoked guanciale. When the bowl of pasta arrive I only had 1 question in my head. Why does it look like a bowl of ramen or thin pan mee with cheese on top. There were barely any guanciale, the noodles barely have any taste but just salt. To further validate my comment of is this even an italian restaurant? The chef honestly need to go back to school and learn how to cook properly and not just a bunch of inedible food. The entire main course wasn't finished. It was basically garbage especially the pasta. I thought probably i didn't not mix it well. I was constantly trying and realise it was just garbage. We inform the waiter that the dish was just horrible. She came back asking us if we would like a smaller bowl of the same pasta. OH HELL NO. We would just like our dessert.Lastly, the saving grace was the tiramisu. It has their name on it GOODDAM Tiramisu.  I would assume it at least taste decent and it was.To be paying Rm 283.80 for at unfinished 3 dishes was basically robbery. I just expected the food to at least be better than what people bragged it to be but we were left disappointed in the end. We went to mamak after that dinner and had cheese naan. that was definitely worth the RM6 I paid.If you are thinking of giving this restaurant a try, go at your own risk or if you are looking for a place with nice ambience and don't care if you are serve garbage then this will be the place for you.The review is my own opinion.
